# E-1722 — Triage: MEMORY.md lessons → endless feature / guide-doc fit

**Findings only.** This classifies which of the endless project's agent-memory
entries look like conversion candidates. It does NOT decide dispositions, design
fixes, or file follow-ups — that is E-1723, which consumes this table.

## Method & coverage

All **140 topic files** in `~/.claude/projects/-…-endless/memory/` were read in
full (body, not just the MEMORY.md one-line index) and classified via a 4-way
fan-out, then normalized in one pass by re-checking every (a)/(d) call against the
live code surfaces (`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, `src/endless/task_cmd.py`,
`docs/guide/`). Categories:

- **(a) endless-feature fit** — could be gated/enforced by the product (hook / CLI
  check / schema-enum) so every user gets it, not just Mike's memory.
- **(b) guide-doc fit** — durable guidance for `endless guide`.
- **(c) stays memory** — pure agent-behavior / generic-tool / writing-style
  feedback with no endless product surface.
- **(d) stale/obsolete** — no longer true; pruning candidate.

**Normalization overrides applied** (subagent first-pass adjusted by me):
- *Plan seeds:* the ship-in-product cluster (`endless-fixes-ship-in-product-…`,
  `ship-in-product-not-machine`) + `gates-not-guardrails` are the **meta-principle
  behind the whole (a) column** → filed (b), high, flagged META.
- *Already-shipped-as-feature* (verified in code — conversion value is low because
  the gate/validator already exists; memory is now reinforcement): `long-form-…`
  & `task-title-shape` (validate_title/validate_description already enforce
  length+verb-first+no-newline), `record-all-actions` (claim-before-write gate),
  `one-task-per-worktree` (worktree gate E-971/E-986), `no-guessed-sqlite3-paths`
  (sqlite-block gate — residual is only extending it), `no-unauthorized-task-type`
  (`task_types` FK + research-gate already validate `--type`).
- `status-unplanned-not-needs-plan`: code no longer emits `needs_plan` and
  `tasks.status` is intentionally free-text (no CHECK, per `no-db-check-constraints`)
  → moved a→**b** (document the vocabulary; a status-enum conversion would fight the
  deliberate free-text design).

Counts: **(a) 31 · (b) 56 · (c) 52 · (d) 1** = 140.

# E-1719 execution status & adjudication

## Phase 1 — DONE, landed + assumed. Phase 2 — 177 applied; +10 pending re-run.

The record-only slice (nullable branch, historical `--ts`, explicit-value
`task.landed`) shipped and the 177 confident landings were applied on main.

## CORRECTION: `validate-db` is NOT clean — but it was already dirty pre-E-1719.
My earlier "validate-db clean" claim was wrong; I never ran it against the real
(polluted) ledger. The dirtiness has three PRE-EXISTING causes, none introduced
by this backfill:
1. Task status/vocab drift (`needs_plan`→`unplanned`, `verify`→`unverified`,
   `in_progress`→`underway`) — the ~341 task "mismatches". This is the actual
   comparison noise, unrelated to landings.
2. Sandbox test-tasks leaking into the real ledger (`UNIQUE ... tasks.id` for
   E-1..E-96, foreign node ids) — every `e-NNNN-verify.sh` doing `task add
   --db sandbox` has polluted the real ledger.
3. `task_landings` can't be projected: the projector SKIPS session events
   (projector.go:108) so its temp `sessions` table is empty — every landing
   with a session_id fails the session FK (E-1443, E-1719 itself, hundreds,
   all predating this work). Separately, ~38 of the backfilled tasks predate
   the event ledger (no `task.created` event, e.g. E-448) so their landings
   fail the task_id FK. Both are pre-existing projector limits; the backfill
   just points 38 more landings at limit #2.

Why the live data is safe regardless: validate-db's pass/fail is the TASK
comparison (the `task_landings` lines are projection warnings, not failures);
the live rows are correct (session NULL, branch NULL, historical dates); and
`rebuild-db` only rebuilds tasks/decisions/decision_relations — it NEVER
rebuilds task_landings, so there is no path that drops the backfilled rows.

Follow-ups worth filing (separate from E-1719): projector should replay session
events + materialize pre-ledger tasks (or validate-db should special-case
task_landings); and the sandbox-events-in-real-ledger pollution.

## Confident 177 — applied. Clean set: all ancestors of main, none reverted
(E-1108 excluded; E-1669 included), 0 already recorded. Distinct ids 126 -> 303.

## The 25 review-bucket ids — FINAL disposition
Criterion: a task gets a landing iff its code actually landed on main (a real
feature/merge commit that is an ancestor of main), incl. code later removed.

ADDED to the driver (10, pending a re-run of `--apply` from main):
- Feature commit, still on main: E-1084 7199f5fa, E-1275 5b4413dc,
  E-1182 e1b25174, E-991 0b0f1d00, E-992 0b0f1d00, E-1002 e372759e.
- Landed then later removed (per Mike's rule): E-917/918/921 cf834b0b
  (removed by E-1711), E-1126 c11ba0a0 (partly removed by E-1582).

EXCLUDED — epic-shaped umbrellas, no single landing commit (their feature
commits belong to child tasks already in the 177): E-971, E-995. Both are
pre-epic-era tasks that would today be epics; their children land individually,
so the parent never "lands". (Retyping them to epic is a separate concern.)

OPEN — Mike's call, not yet decided: E-1333 (real commit but docs/guide, not
code) and E-1137 (the task's landed work was itself a revert).

EXCLUDED — plan-only / bare-mention, no feature commit: E-894, E-993, E-1031,
E-1085, E-1113, E-1129, E-1186, E-1272, E-1335, E-1037, E-1509. Plus N/A:
decisions D-958/1007/1094/1175/1199/1361/1373; orphan E-783.

## Driver: tests/tasks/e-1719-backfill.sh (187 pairs = 177 + 10)
Idempotent: dedups against task_landings each run, so re-running `--apply` emits
only not-yet-recorded ids (verified: 10 emit, then 0). Node id = machine node
(no ba15). Run from the MAIN checkout (refuses worktrees).

payload.title: Fix projector failing all task_landings inserts (sessions unreplayed, pre-ledger tasks absent)
payload.description: endless-go event validate-db (and any ledger->DB projection) fails to insert nearly every task_landings row, so projection(ledger) != live DB for landings. Two causes: (1) the projector skips session events (projector.go:108), so the temp sessions table is empty and every landing carrying a session_id fails the session_id FK; (2) tasks predating the event ledger have no task.created event, so the projector can't materialize them and their landings fail the task_id FK. Surfaced by E-1719's historical backfill but affects ALL landings (E-1443, E-1719 itself, hundreds). Live task_landings is correct and rebuild-db never rebuilds task_landings (no data loss) — but validate-db is noisy/misleading for landings. Fix direction: replay session events into the projection (an ensureSession mirroring ensureProject) and/or stub pre-ledger tasks, or make validate-db special-case task_landings.

payload.title: Isolate sandbox ledger writes so --db sandbox writes db-ledger to the sandbox, not the real project
payload.description: The E-1281 sandbox isolates DB writes (--db sandbox / XDG) but NOT ledger writes. emit_event resolves project_root from the projects table (the real checkout) and appends+commits event JSONL to the real .endless/db-ledger/ regardless of --db sandbox. So every sandbox operation — e.g. every 'endless task add --db sandbox' in a tests/tasks/*-verify.sh — permanently writes test-task events (ids 1,2,3... under per-sandbox node ids) into the PRODUCTION ledger, colliding with real E-1..E-96 and making validate-db/rebuild-db noisy. Fix: in sandbox mode route the ledger to a sandbox-local db-ledger dir (mirror the DB isolation), or make sandbox emits DB-only. Surfaced by E-1719's validate-db check. Do this BEFORE the cleanup task, else the leak keeps re-accruing.

payload.title: Excise leaked sandbox test-task events from the real db-ledger
payload.description: The real .endless/db-ledger/ contains a large volume of leaked sandbox/test events (task.created for ids 1..96+ under foreign per-sandbox node ids), from the unisolated sandbox ledger (E-1729). They collide with real tasks and produce the UNIQUE tasks.id / FK noise in validate-db. Excise them from the ledger CAREFULLY — the ledger is the DB's write-ahead log, so mis-editing corrupts the DB: identify the sandbox-node segments/lines, remove them, then re-derive + validate. Must run AFTER E-1729's isolation fix lands, otherwise new pollution re-accrues.

payload.title: Add endless verb CLI to set and show a verb's category
payload.description: Add CLI support for the verb category mechanism that replaces the per-verb completable boolean (per E-1658): let a user set and show a verb's category (action/investigation, multi-value for dual verbs) without hand-editing verbs.jsonl, mirroring the existing endless verb add/list/remove shape. E-1658 currently lists 'endless verb (set/show category)' only as an inline touch-point, so this carves the CLI slice out as its own deliverable.

# E-1729 — Isolate the sandbox ledger

## Problem
`--db sandbox` (E-1281) isolates the DB (`ConfigDir()/endless.db`) but NOT the
event ledger. Every emit resolves its ledger dir from `--project-root` — the
real checkout, which `emit_event` looks up from the projects table — so sandbox
emits append + git-commit event JSONL into the production
`~/Projects/endless/.endless/db-ledger/`. Sandbox/test tasks (ids 1,2,3… under
per-sandbox node ids) therefore permanently pollute the real ledger, collide
with real E-1..E-96, and produce the `UNIQUE tasks.id` / FK noise in
`validate-db`. (Excising the already-leaked events is E-1730, blocked on this.)

## Decision (single path)
Route a sandbox's ledger to a sandbox-local dir and skip its git commit.
**Go-only change; no Python change; no migration.**

- **Sandbox ledger location:** `<ConfigDir()>/.endless/db-ledger/` — same
  `.endless/db-ledger` layout as the real project, but under the sandbox's own
  config dir (in sandbox mode `ConfigDir()` is
  `~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/e-NNN/endless`), a sibling of the sandbox
  `endless.db`.
- **No git commit in the sandbox.** The sandbox dir is not a git repo and is
  disposable — nothing rebuilds from its ledger across machines — so the
  per-segment `git add/commit` (E-1206) is skipped in sandbox mode rather than
  `git init`-ing every sandbox.

## Why not DB-only emits (ruled out)
The DB is a projection of the ledger; a DB write with no ledger event can't be
rebuilt, and `rebuild-db` in a sandbox would wipe all sandbox state. Incompatible
with events-authoritative. The ledger must exist; it just has to be isolated.

## Implementation (all in `internal/eventcmd/event.go`; no events-package signature changes)
Every ledger read/write already funnels through this file — 3 `events.NewWriter`
callsites (incl. the writer reused by `makeDerivedEmitter`) and 2
`events.ProjectToTempDB` callsites (validate-db, rebuild-db) — so the fix is
contained here.

1. Add one helper in `eventcmd`:
   `ledgerRoot(projectRoot string) string` → returns `monitor.ConfigDir()` when
   `monitor.IsSandboxActive()`, else `projectRoot`. (`NewWriter`/`ReadAllEvents`
   append `.endless/db-ledger` to whatever root they get, so the sandbox ledger
   lands at `ConfigDir()/.endless/db-ledger`. `NewWriter` already `MkdirAll`s the
   dir on first write, so the sandbox ledger dir is created automatically.)
2. Pass `ledgerRoot(*projectRoot)` in place of `*projectRoot` at all 3
   `NewWriter` callsites and both `ProjectToTempDB` callsites. This is what makes
   `validate-db --db sandbox` / `rebuild-db --db sandbox` read the SANDBOX ledger.
3. Guard the 3 `CommitLedgerSegment(...)` calls with
   `if !monitor.IsSandboxActive() { ... }`. Real emits commit exactly as today.

No Python change: `emit_event` keeps passing `--project-root` (real checkout) and
`--config-dir <sandbox>` (via `go_db_context_args`). `IsSandboxActive()` is driven
by `ConfigDir()` (which honors `--config-dir`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), so the Go side
detects the sandbox and ignores `projectRoot` for the ledger automatically.

Confirm no ledger callers exist outside `eventcmd` before finishing (grep
`NewWriter`/`ReadAllEvents`/`CommitLedgerSegment`; today they are all here).

## Out of scope / non-goals
- Excising already-leaked events from the real ledger — that is **E-1730**
  (blocked_by this).
- No migration/back-compat: existing sandbox DBs simply begin a fresh (empty)
  sandbox ledger. A stale sandbox with no ledger projects to empty (fine —
  disposable); recreate the sandbox if a populated ledger is wanted.
- The normal `worktree land` ledger path (real, main-pinned) is unchanged.

## Verify (`tests/tasks/e-1729-verify.sh`, fleet convention + go unit)
1. Snapshot the real `~/Projects/endless/.endless/db-ledger/` line count and
   `git rev-parse HEAD`.
2. Run `endless task add "probe" --db sandbox` (and a status change).
3. Assert: (a) a new segment/lines appeared under
   `<sandbox>/.endless/db-ledger/`; (b) the real ledger line count is UNCHANGED;
   (c) the real repo HEAD is UNCHANGED (no commit); (d)
   `endless task show <id> --db sandbox` sees the task; (e)
   `endless-go event validate-db` in the sandbox reads the sandbox ledger.
4. Go unit test for `ledgerRoot`/`IsSandboxActive` (sandbox vs real).
5. `just test` + `go test ./...` green.

fields.text:
# Research brief: endless's event-ledger target routing + git-commit constraints

## Why
E-1729 surfaced that `--db sandbox` isolates the DB but NOT the ledger, so
dev/test emits pollute the real `.endless/db-ledger/`. The naive fix ("sandbox
skips the git commit") breaks the <1% case where we are testing endless's OWN
ledger/commit machinery and therefore NEED a real, committing, isolated ledger.
Before deciding the policy (a follow-on brainstorm), map the FACTS.
**Deliver facts, not a recommendation** — "what should we do" is the brainstorm's job.

## Questions to answer (facts, each with file.go:Symbol references)
1. **Write paths.** Every code path that appends to a ledger and/or git-commits a
   segment: `events.NewWriter` callers, `events.CommitLedgerSegment` callers,
   `worktree land` auto-commit (commit.go / canAmend), the hook binary, the
   channel MCP, anything else. For each: how it resolves (a) the ledger dir,
   (b) the project root, (c) whether/where it commits.
2. **Read paths.** `events.ReadAllEvents` / `events.ProjectToTempDB` callers
   (`validate-db`, `rebuild-db`, projection): how each resolves the ledger location.
3. **Location resolution, end to end.** Python `emit_event` project_root (projects
   table) + `--config-dir` / `go_db_context_args`; Go `monitor.ConfigDir()` /
   `IsSandboxActive()` / `--project-root`; and how DB location vs ledger location
   relate today.
4. **Git-commit coupling (E-1206).** What `CommitLedgerSegment` does and why; what
   depends on the commits (canAmend rewrite, `worktree land`, backups, recovery,
   `just land`); what breaks if a ledger dir is not a git repo or commits are skipped.
5. **Sandbox mechanics (E-1281).** What a sandbox isolates today (DB via XDG /
   config-dir) vs not (ledger); how sandboxes are created/destroyed; whether the
   sandbox dir is a git repo.
6. **Event-sourcing invariants.** What "events-authoritative" requires (ledger =
   source of truth, DB = projection) and what `rebuild-db` / `validate-db` assume,
   so any isolation option can be checked against them.
7. **The <1% product-testing case.** How endless's own ledger/commit code is tested
   today (e.g. `tests/tasks/e-1719-verify.sh`'s throwaway `git init` project root);
   what those harnesses need from the ledger (real commits). Catalog the patterns.
8. **Pollution evidence.** Quantify the sandbox events already in the real ledger
   (count, node ids, id ranges) — grounds E-1730 and shows blast radius.
9. **Prior decisions.** What E-1281, E-1206, E-1368, E-1513, E-1719, E-1729, E-1730
   each already locked in about ledger location/commit, and whether ledger isolation
   was ever discussed.

## Deliverable (in the task outcome)
A factual map answering 1-9 with `file.go:Symbol` references, plus a plain
statement of the **decision space** the facts imply (the distinct options for
"which ledger does an emit target, and who decides") WITHOUT choosing one. That
map feeds a follow-on `brainstorm` task where we decide the policy, which then
re-plans E-1729.

## Out of scope
- Deciding the policy (brainstorm's job) or recommending an option.
- Implementing anything / touching the ledger (E-1729 fix, E-1730 cleanup).

fields.outcome:
# E-1732 findings — Ledger-target routing (main vs sandbox vs test) and git-commit constraints

Factual map for the follow-on policy brainstorm (which re-plans E-1729). No recommendation is made.
All references verified against worktree `task/1732-research-endless-s-ledger-target-routing` (forked from main a0b3f627).

## 1. Write paths

**There is exactly one ledger writer in the system: the Go `endless-go event emit` path.** Everything else funnels into it.

- `internal/events/writer.go:46 NewWriter(projectRoot, nodeHex)` — ledger dir is a hard-coded join: `<projectRoot>/.endless/db-ledger` (`LedgerDirName`, writer.go:29). Segment files `db-entries-<nodeHex>-NNNNNN.jsonl`, rotated at `DefaultMaxEventsPerSegment = 500` (writer.go:23). `Writer.Append` (writer.go:72) is an `O_APPEND` one-line write; the writer itself is git-agnostic and `MkdirAll`s the dir.
- **All `NewWriter` callers** are in `internal/eventcmd/event.go` (verified by grep; the only other importer of `internal/events`, `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go:134`, is read-only): event.go:192 (create/pre-alloc flow), event.go:268 (update/delete flow), event.go:424 (`runProjectNextRevise`). The derived-emitter closure `makeDerivedEmitter` (event.go:323) reuses the caller's writer to append `epic.status_derived` (event.go:357).
- **`CommitLedgerSegment` has FOUR callsites, not three** — event.go:207, :278, :361 (inside `makeDerivedEmitter`), :436. E-1729's drafted plan says "the 3 CommitLedgerSegment calls"; that count is stale/wrong and the re-plan should absorb the fourth (the epic-derivation one).
- **Write ordering (events-authoritative):** DB write-lock first (`PreAllocateTaskID`/`BeginImmediate` do `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `internal/events/executor.go:117-137`), then ledger append, then `CommitLedgerSegment`, then the SQL mutation + `COMMIT`. A commit failure aborts before the DB mutation — but **after** the JSONL line is on disk (see §4).
- **`--project-root` is a required flag on `event emit`** (event.go:62,98-100). The Go side does no resolution of its own; resolution happens upstream in Python.
- **Python `emit_event`** (`src/endless/event_bridge.py:77`) never writes the ledger itself; it shells out to Go (event_bridge.py:204-228) passing `*config.go_db_context_args()` (→ `--config-dir`) **and** `--project-root`. Project root resolution (event_bridge.py:184-198): `SELECT path FROM projects WHERE name = ?` **against whichever DB is active** — deliberately the registered main checkout, not cwd; falls back to `Path.cwd()` only for unregistered projects. Note the routing consequence: a sandbox DB's `projects.path` is seeded from the **main** DB's row by `seedFromWorktree` (`internal/sandboxcmd/seed_worktree.go:44-45`), so sandbox emits resolve the **real** checkout as their ledger root. This single seeded value is what points sandbox ledger writes at the production ledger.
- **`node_id`**: `_get_or_create_node_id` (event_bridge.py:283) reads `config.CONFIG_FILE` = `<resolved config dir>/config.json` and mints `secrets.token_hex(2)` (4 hex chars) on first use. Real node = `a7f3` in `~/.config/endless/config.json`; each sandbox mints its own node id in `<sandbox>/endless/config.json`. 4 hex chars = 65,536-value space (collision odds grow with sandbox count; ~40 sandboxes ≈ 1.2% birthday collision).
- **`worktree land`** (`src/endless/worktree_cmd.py:1478 land_worktree`) has three ledger-adjacent steps: Step 3 auto-commits accumulated dirt matching `AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS` (worktree_cmd.py:54: `.endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl`, verbs files) as `"Endless: auto-record session activity"` — a plain, non-amendable commit on `main_root`; Step 3.7 `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits` (worktree_cmd.py:258) strips orphaned `"Endless: record ledger entry"` commits at branch base (exists because `canAmend` rewrites ledger-tip SHAs on main, E-1342); Step 6 `_record_landing` (worktree_cmd.py:1434) emits `task.landed` through the normal `emit_event` → Go path.
- **The hook binary does NOT write the ledger** — `internal/hookcmd/` has no `internal/events` import. Hook-attributed events go through Python `emit_event` with `actor_kind="hook"` (`_ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED`, event_bridge.py:24).
- **The channel MCP does NOT write the ledger** — `internal/channelcmd/channel.go` is an HTTP notify/inbox server; `src/endless/channel_cmd.py` has no `emit_event` calls.

## 2. Read paths

- `internal/events/reader.go:16 ReadAllEvents(projectRoot)` — reads `<projectRoot>/.endless/db-ledger`, globs ALL `db-entries-*.jsonl` regardless of node, merges, sorts by `evt.TS` (kairos; lexicographic = causal). Missing dir → `nil, nil`. **Its only caller is `ProjectToTempDB`** (projector.go:31).
- `internal/events/projector.go:28 ProjectToTempDB(projectRoot)` — replays into a temp SQLite DB at `<projectRoot>/.endless/projection-temp.db`; errors on zero events (projector.go:36-38).
- **Callers, both in `internal/eventcmd/event.go`:** `runValidateDB` (event.go:460) and `runRebuildDB` (event.go:520). Both take a **required `--project-root` flag** for the ledger and resolve the live DB independently via `monitor.DB()` (event.go:486, :550). `validate-db` compares and mutates nothing; `rebuild-db --confirm` ATTACHes the temp DB and **deletes + reinserts the project's entire `tasks`/`decisions`** from the projection (event.go:571-595).
- No Python or justfile caller invokes `validate-db`/`rebuild-db`; they are manual/test-invoked.

## 3. Location resolution, end to end

**DB location and ledger location are resolved by two entirely independent mechanisms.**

- **DB** = `monitor.ConfigDir()/endless.db` (`internal/monitor/db.go:100-105 DBPath`). `ConfigDir()` precedence (db.go:61-70): explicit `--config-dir` (consumed by `ConsumeDBContextFlag`, db.go:196, first thing in `cmd/endless-go/main.go:61`) → self-detected sandbox → `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/endless` → `~/.config/endless`.
  - `SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox()` (db.go:289-313, E-1368): fires only when no explicit context; derives `e-NNN` from the `/.endless/worktrees/e-NNN` cwd marker; requires `projectIsSelfDev(root)` (db.go:319-331 reads `<root>/.endless/config.json` `self_dev`) AND the sandbox dir existing on disk; routes via `setDetectedContextDir` — deliberately weaker than the explicit flag, so `ForceRealDB()` (hook, db.go:107-126) and `PinMainDB()` (channel/tmux, db.go:180-186) still win (the E-1450 split: session/pane/channel state stays on the real DB even in a sandbox; config.json + logs follow the sandbox).
  - `IsSandboxActive()` (db.go:90-97): true iff `ConfigDir()` resolves under `CacheDir()/sandboxes`.
  - Python mirror: `apply_db_choice("main"|"sandbox")` (`src/endless/config.py:248-268`); `sandbox_config_dir` = `<cache>/endless/sandboxes/<e-NNN>/endless` (config.py:204-213); `set_db_context` (config.py:236-245); `go_db_context_args()` → `["--config-dir", RESOLVED_CONFIG_DIR]` (config.py:308-318); E-1513 re-exec into the worktree's Python source for `--db sandbox` (`src/endless/cli.py:200-206`); E-1429 gate `require_db_context` / Go `guardWorktreeDBContext` (config.py:292-305; db.go:404-419) refuses ambiguous DB opens inside a self-dev worktree.
- **Ledger** = `<projectRoot>/.endless/db-ledger`, where `projectRoot` = the `--project-root` flag = Python's `projects.path` lookup (§1). `go_db_context_args()` threads only DB location; **nothing anywhere threads a ledger location** — it is always derived from project root. `--db main|sandbox` therefore moves the DB and leaves the ledger fixed on the real checkout. This is the E-1729 bug mechanism, stated in code at `internal/events/commit.go:135-138` (sandbox routing affects the DB only).

## 4. Git-commit coupling (E-1206)

**What `CommitLedgerSegment` does** (`internal/events/commit.go:43` → `commitPaths`, commit.go:78):
1. `ensureGitRepo` (commit.go:118): `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`; not a work tree → error `"project root %q is not a git work tree"`.
2. `ensureMainCheckout` (commit.go:139, E-1309): `--git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` differ (linked worktree) → refuse. Auto-commits land on main, never a task branch.
3. `canAmend` (commit.go:169): amend iff HEAD subject == `LedgerCommitSubject` (`"Endless: record ledger entry"`, commit.go:24) AND HEAD not reachable from any other ref AND index clean modulo the ledger glob. Then `git add` + `git commit -o <segment>` with `--amend --no-edit` or `-m`.
4. Runs with `sanitizedGitEnv` (commit.go:258) stripping `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/etc.

**Why it exists:** E-1206 (confirmed) — every ledger write becomes git history at write time (durability; no accumulating dirt between lands); the amend strategy bounds commit count to one rolling ledger commit between feature commits, never rewriting pushed history. E-1206 explicitly decided fail-loudly, including "project root is not a git repo → fail; soften only when beta testers make it concrete."

**What depends on the commits:**
- `worktree land` Step 3.7 orphan-drop (`worktree_cmd.py:258-266`) exists solely because `canAmend` rewrites main's ledger-tip SHA, orphaning branches forked from the old SHA (E-1342).
- Land Step 3 assumes db-ledger dirt is committable (`AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS`).
- The land rebase-failure recovery message (`worktree_cmd.py:1626-1637`) instructs `git checkout <base> -- .endless/db-ledger/*.jsonl` — assumes ledger files are git-tracked.
- Multi-dev sync: committed segments are how another machine gets the ledger (per-node segment naming exists to avoid git merge conflicts — recorded in the ledger itself, event for E-906).
- NOT coupled: `endless db backup` is a SQLite `VACUUM INTO` (event.go:758); `validate-db`/`rebuild-db` read working-tree JSONL, not git history; `just land` delegates to `worktree land` (justfile:227-247).

**Failure behavior — hard, with a known stray-line hazard:** every git failure propagates (`runGit`, commit.go:225) → emit exits non-zero → Python raises `click.ClickException` (event_bridge.py:229-231). But `Writer.Append` has already run, so **a failed commit leaves the JSONL line on disk with no commit and no DB mutation** — exactly E-1665's observed pollution-by-failed-emit. There is **no code path that skips the commit**; it is unconditional after every append.

## 5. Sandbox mechanics (E-1281)

- **Create:** `just dev-sandbox-init` (justfile:414-439, refuses main checkout) → `endless-go sandbox init --mode worktree <e-NNN>` + `sandbox bind <worktree> <e-NNN>`. Auto-invoked on claim/spawn by `_maybe_auto_sandbox_bind` (`worktree_cmd.py:1285`), gated on `config.project_is_self_dev` (config.py:118-130); failures warn, don't abort.
  - `initCmd` (`internal/sandboxcmd/init.go:10`): modes `empty`|`worktree` only (`seed`/`clone` unimplemented); idempotent unless `--force`.
  - `Provision` (`internal/sandboxcmd/sandbox.go:74`): plain `os.Mkdir` under `CacheDir()/sandboxes` + `.sandbox-meta.json`. **The sandbox dir is NOT a git repo** — no `git init` anywhere in sandboxcmd; `seedFromWorktree` runs only read-only `git rev-parse` to find the main checkout.
  - `seedFromWorktree` (`seed_worktree.go:30`): creates `<dir>/endless/endless.db` with `schema.SQL`, inserts a `projects` row **copied from the main DB (path = real checkout)** and a `sessions` row, writes `<dir>/endless/config.json` from a hardcoded default.
  - `bindCmd` (`internal/sandboxcmd/bind.go:15`): writes `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<sandboxDir>` into `<worktree>/.claude/settings.json` env block; sets skip-worktree.
- **Destroy:** `destroyCmd` (`internal/sandboxcmd/destroy.go:10`): refuses if live writers hold files open (unless `--force`), then `os.RemoveAll`. **Destroying a sandbox erases its node_id mapping** — the real ledger's leaked segments from destroyed sandboxes become orphan node ids (see §8).
- **What it isolates:** the DB, config.json, and logs (everything under `ConfigDir()`). **Not the ledger** (§3), and deliberately not session/pane/channel state (E-1450 pins those to the real DB).
- **`self_dev` gates:** sandbox auto-provisioning (worktree_cmd.py:1298), Go cwd self-detect (db.go:298), the E-1429 DB-context refusal (db.go:404-419), hook-binary selection (db.go:343-378), self-dev land behaviors (worktree_cmd.py:1338-1352).

## 6. Event-sourcing invariants

- **Events-authoritative write contract:** lock → ledger line → git commit → SQL, per the comments at event.go:145-148/:202/:262/:418 and `executor.go:124-128`. A losing concurrent writer fails at `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before writing an orphan line.
- **Projection assumptions:** replay is ordered **solely by kairos TS** (reader.go:44-47) — the envelope has no sequence number (`Event`, event.go:17-26). Entity ids are replayed **verbatim with no collision handling** (`projector.go:146 mustParseInt64(evt.Entity.ID)`); ids are DB-scoped pre-allocations, so two DBs (main + a sandbox) freely allocate the same id for different entities — which is precisely why leaked sandbox events collide (UNIQUE/FK noise). `rebuild-db --confirm` assumes ONE complete ledger per project: it deletes and reinserts the whole project from the single projection (event.go:571-595).
- **No snapshots, no upcasting yet:** projection always replays from event zero; `V != 1` is hard-rejected (event.go:274-276). The upcasting pipeline is pending (E-1671); today the projector is leniently hand-coded for legacy shapes (projector.go:129-135, :568-580) because "the events ledger records history and cannot be rewritten".
- **Multi-writer:** one dir, per-node segment files, merged by TS at read. A second ledger *directory* has no support anywhere: `ReadAllEvents` reads exactly one root; there is no cross-dir merge; and `CommitLedgerSegment` refuses roots that aren't the main checkout of a git repo.

## 7. The <1% product-testing case — how ledger/commit machinery is tested today

Five distinct harness patterns exist (no shared harness; the shell ones self-describe as the "E-1596 ad-hoc-prototype shape"):

1. **Throwaway `git init` repo as `--project-root` + separate temp DB via `--config-dir`/XDG** — the pattern for anything that exercises the real emit path, because that path *requires* a committable main-checkout repo. Used by `tests/tasks/e-1719-verify.sh:100-153` (Section C: `mktemp -d`, `git init`, `--allow-empty` commit with pinned `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, then `event emit ... --project-root "$REPO" --config-dir "$GODIR"`), `tests/tasks/e-1664-verify.sh:116-151` (`make_ledger_repo`, comment cites E-1309), and Go `internal/events/commit_test.go:26-34` (`initRepo`: `t.TempDir()` + `git init` + identity + initial commit; full amend/pushed/worktree-refusal matrix) and `internal/eventcmd/epic_derivation_test.go:104,189`. **Needs: real git commits on a real repo.**
2. **Fabricated JSONL segments, no git** — `internal/eventcmd/event_test.go:112-127 writeLedgerEvent` hand-writes segment lines for `validate-db`/`rebuild-db` tests. **Needs: only a directory with segment files** (read side never touches git).
3. **DB-only** — executor-level tests against a `t.TempDir()` SQLite file (`internal/events/task_landed_test.go`); no ledger at all.
4. **pytest `isolated_env`** — `tests/conftest.py:13-77` monkeypatches CONFIG_DIR/DB_PATH AND exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` so spawned Go subprocesses share the temp DB; stubs the E-1513 re-exec.
5. **Real-routing assertions** — `e-1628-verify.sh`, `e-1368-verify.sh`, `e-1662-verify.sh` drive the actual sandbox/main dirs to assert routing/pinning, no throwaway repo.

**No test today relies on a sandbox hosting a ledger or on sandbox emits committing.** The real-commit need is met exclusively by pattern 1's throwaway repos. E-1665 (open brainstorm) exists because pattern 1 is a convention you can forget — a hand-run `event emit --project-root <real-repo>` pollutes before the guard rejects it (§4).

## 8. Pollution evidence (working tree, real ledger, measured 2026-07-04)

- Real ledger `~/Projects/endless/.endless/db-ledger/`: **49 segment files, 4,744 lines, 42 distinct node ids.**
- Real node `a7f3` (`~/.config/endless/config.json`): 8 segments, **3,673 lines**, real task ids up to 1732.
- **Foreign: 41 segments / 41 node ids / 1,071 lines (~23% of the ledger).** 37 of the 41 map 1:1 to a live sandbox's `<sandbox>/endless/config.json` node_id (e.g. e-1542→86eb, e-1544→02ef, e-1567→1d2e, e-1577→d1b2, worktree-e-1281→648e). 4 are orphans (sandbox destroyed or other origin): `1421` (11 lines, test tasks at real-id range 1034-1039 — an early sandbox seeded with real-range ids), `9000` (16 lines, **real** early events E-805/E-900..909 from the ledger rollout era — NOT pollution), `abcd` (5 duplicate `task.landed` for 1628), `d082` (4 lines, ids 1-3).
- **Node id alone does not cleanly separate pollution:**
  - Segment `86eb` (sandbox e-1542) interleaves test `task.created` ids 1-5 with **real-looking `task.landed` events for E-1542 itself**; `abcd` is all `task.landed` 1628; `b745` (e-1588) is a `session_status.recorded`. Foreign-node excision would also remove these.
  - Sandbox `worktree-e-1507`'s config carries node_id **`a7f3` — identical to the real node** — so any emits it made are interleaved inside the real `a7f3` segments, indistinguishable by node id.
  - Node ids are 4 hex chars minted per config dir (§1); orphaning on `sandbox destroy` and birthday collisions are structural.
- 5 sandboxes hold node_ids with no leaked segment (3c00/e-1555, 1d41/e-1596, acce/wt-1337, 587e/wt-1469, 59d1/wt-1517) — a node id is minted on first emit attempt, not first leak.
- **validate-db today** (run read-only from the main checkout): `4744 events replayed, 846 tasks created, 2377 updated, 52 deleted`; **835 warnings** (FK 787 failures on `task_landing` inserts + UNIQUE `task.created` collisions); `Validation: 0 tasks compared`; **792 tasks listed "only in projected"**. The output is dominated by noise, which is what surfaced E-1729 during E-1719 verification.
- Prior measurement for the **committed** ledger (E-1710 audit, main HEAD then 531942a4): 4,450 events / 47 segments, of which ~36 segments (~1,500 events, ~1/3) are test-fixture ledgers reusing real ids 1..~150 (recorded in E-1716/E-1041). The two counts differ in method (fixture-event count vs foreign-node line count) and time; both are cited here as measured.

## 9. Prior decisions (what's already locked in)

| Task | Status | What it locked in about ledger location / commits |
|---|---|---|
| E-1206 | confirmed | Write-time auto-commit of every ledger append on main; amend-based rolling commit; **fail loudly, incl. "not a git repo → fail"** (softening explicitly deferred); ledger = the DB's WAL. |
| E-1309 (via code) | landed | Ledger auto-commits refuse linked worktrees; must land on the main checkout (`ensureMainCheckout`). |
| E-1342 (via code) | landed | Land drops orphaned amendable ledger commits — a direct dependency on the amend behavior. |
| E-1281 | assumed | Sandbox isolates the **DB** via XDG/config-dir; per-project `self_dev` opt-in; sandbox = plain dir under `~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/`; "start fresh, existing prod-DB pollution stays put". **Ledger isolation was not discussed** — the plan text addresses DB pollution only. |
| E-1368 | assumed | Go binaries self-detect the sandbox from cwd; explicit `--config-dir` wins; detected context is weaker than hook/channel pins. |
| E-1513 | assumed | Python re-execs into the worktree source for `--db sandbox`. |
| E-1450 (via code) | landed | The split: DB sandbox-routed; session/pane/channel state pinned to the real DB; config.json/logs follow the sandbox. |
| E-1719 | unverified | `--record-only` backfill; its verify harness is the throwaway-repo pattern; its `validate-db` runs surfaced the leak → filed E-1729/E-1730. |
| E-1729 | revisit | Has a **drafted** decision (sandbox ledger at `ConfigDir()/.endless/db-ledger`, skip commit in sandbox, Go-only in eventcmd; DB-only emits ruled out as violating events-authoritative) — awaiting this research + the brainstorm. Its callsite count is stale: **4** `CommitLedgerSegment` calls exist, not 3 (§1). |
| E-1730 | unplanned, blocked by E-1729 | Excise the leaked events from the real ledger, carefully (WAL). |
| E-1710 | completed | Committed-ledger audit: no systemic WAL loss; characterized the fixture pollution (~36/47 segments). |
| E-1716 | unplanned | **The fix for committed pollution is NOT deletion/rewrite** — neutralize via an appended revert/tombstone the projector skips (first consumer of E-1720). Note: this stands in tension with E-1730's "remove them" framing; the brainstorm should reconcile excision vs tombstoning. |
| E-1720 | unplanned | The revert/tombstone mechanism itself (git-revert-style appended entry). |
| E-1665 | unplanned brainstorm | Safe-by-construction testing of the emit/integrity path (dry-run / read-only verb) so direct invocation physically cannot pollute. |
| E-1671 | (parent pipeline) | Upcasting pipeline; its brief already names a "project/machine-user **two-ledger scope split** enforced at emit" — prior art for multiple ledgers with distinct scopes. |
| E-1041 | open | Catalogs the three rebuild-db warning classes (pre-event-system FK gaps; MAX(id)+1 reuse; fixture-id collisions). |

**Was ledger isolation ever discussed before?** No — E-1281's plan is DB-only; the first explicit treatment of ledger targeting is E-1729 (2026-07-04). The adjacent prior art is E-1716/E-1720 (append-only neutralization of pollution already committed) and E-1671 (two-ledger scope split at emit).

## Decision space the facts imply (options only — choosing is the brainstorm's job)

The policy question decomposes into four independent axes:

**A. Where does a sandbox/test emit's ledger line land?**
1. Real project ledger (status quo — the bug).
2. Sandbox-local ledger, `ConfigDir()/.endless/db-ledger` (E-1729's draft). Mechanism exists: every read/write already funnels through `internal/eventcmd/event.go`; swapping the root at 3 `NewWriter` + 2 `ProjectToTempDB` callsites re-targets everything.
3. No ledger for sandbox emits (DB-only). Already ruled out in E-1729's draft as incompatible with events-authoritative (`rebuild-db` in a sandbox would wipe sandbox state); recorded here as considered-and-rejected.
4. Re-point via the data, not the code: the ledger root is just `projects.path` in the **active** DB (§1). Seeding the sandbox's `projects.path` to the sandbox dir would re-route emits with zero Go changes — but `path` is also used for other purposes, and the commit path would then hard-fail (sandbox isn't a git repo), so this axis interacts with axis B.

**B. Commit behavior for a non-real ledger.** Facts constraining it: `CommitLedgerSegment` fails hard without a main-checkout git repo (§4); the sandbox dir is not a git repo (§5); nothing downstream (amend/land/recovery/multi-dev sync) cares about a *sandbox* ledger's git history — those dependencies are all about the real repo (§4). Options: skip commits when `IsSandboxActive()` (E-1729 draft); `git init` each sandbox to keep the code path uniform; or make commit-vs-skip an explicit property of the ledger target rather than of sandbox detection.

**C. Who decides the target?** (a) Implicit sandbox self-detection — `IsSandboxActive()` derived from `ConfigDir()` (E-1729 draft: no Python change, hooks/tests inherit it); (b) an explicit flag (`--ledger-root` or similar) making the target a stated input like `--project-root` is today — which is also what every existing test harness effectively does by hand (§7); (c) the DB's `projects.path` (option A4). Fact to weigh: today NO mechanism threads a ledger location anywhere — it is 100% derived — so any explicit option adds a new surface.

**D. The <1% real-commit testing case.** Facts: that case is served today by throwaway `git init` repos via `--project-root`, in both Go tests (`commit_test.go:initRepo`) and shell verifies (§7), and never by sandboxes. So "sandbox skips commits" removes nothing those harnesses use — but E-1665 documents that the throwaway-repo convention is forgettable and the failure mode of forgetting it is exactly this pollution. Whether the fix folds a safe default into the emit path (E-1665's question) or stays a test convention is part of the brainstorm.

**Read-side symmetry (applies to any option):** whatever root emits write to, `validate-db`/`rebuild-db` under `--db sandbox` must read the same root, or sandbox rebuilds replay the wrong ledger (E-1729's draft covers this via the same helper at both `ProjectToTempDB` callsites).

**Cleanup interaction:** E-1730 (excise) vs E-1716/E-1720 (append-only tombstoning) prescribe different treatments for pollution already in the ledger; §8 shows node-id-based excision would clip some real-looking events (`task.landed` 1542/1628, the a7f3-node sandbox) — a fact the cleanup decision needs regardless of the isolation policy chosen.

# Brainstorm: ledger-target routing policy

This is a discussion task. The deliverable is the brainstorm's results in this task's
outcome — the decided policy, per-use-case behavior, rejected options with reasons, and
any genuine conflicts. Do not implement anything.

## Step 1 — Read the research

Read E-1732's findings first: `endless task show E-1732 --outcome --db main`.
That is the factual map: every ledger write/read path, the git-commit coupling and its
dependents, sandbox mechanics, event-sourcing invariants, the test-harness patterns,
the measured pollution, prior decisions, and the decision space (axes A–D: where a
sandbox/test emit's ledger line lands; commit behavior for a non-real ledger; who
decides the target; the real-commit testing case).

## Step 2 — Discuss with Mike

Work the decision space with Mike in chat, not solo:

1. For every approach in the decision space (and any new approach that surfaces in
   discussion), lay out the pros and cons.
2. For each approach, explain concretely how the ledger should and will work in each
   use-case:
   - real emits from the main checkout (CLI and hook-attributed)
   - emits from a self-dev worktree session routed to a sandbox (`--db sandbox` /
     cwd self-detect)
   - `worktree land` (auto-commit of ledger dirt + the `task.landed` emit)
   - `validate-db` / `rebuild-db` in both main and sandbox contexts
   - test harnesses that exercise the emit/commit machinery (today: throwaway
     `git init` repos as `--project-root`)
   - multi-dev / multi-node sync via committed segments
3. Identify any situations that are truly in conflict — requirements no single
   approach can satisfy simultaneously — versus ones that are merely undecided, and
   state them explicitly. Include the cleanup tension the research surfaced: E-1730's
   excision vs E-1716/E-1720's append-only tombstoning.

## Step 3 — Record and hand off

Write the brainstorm results into this task's outcome. Then the decided policy
re-plans E-1729 (and informs E-1730's cleanup). Do not re-plan E-1729 without Mike's
explicit go-ahead in the discussion.

fields.outcome:
# E-1733 brainstorm results — ledger-target routing policy

Decided with Mike, 2026-07-04. Works from E-1732's factual map.

## Decided policy

1. **The ledger lives next to whichever DB is active.** Main DB → real project ledger, auto-committed on main at write time (unchanged; E-1206/ED-901). Sandbox DB → `db-ledger/` inside the sandbox dir, next to its `endless.db`.
2. **The sandbox ledger never touches git.** It sits in the cache dir outside any repo — nothing to commit, no merge machinery, erased atomically with `sandbox destroy`. The DB and its WAL live and die together.
3. **One in-code resolver decides the ledger target** — root directory plus commit-or-not, resolved once alongside the existing DB-context resolution. All four `CommitLedgerSegment` callsites (E-1729's draft says three; the epic-derivation emitter is the fourth) and both `ProjectToTempDB` callsites ask it. No flag, no env var, no config file.
4. **Reads are symmetric**: `validate-db`/`rebuild-db` replay whatever ledger the active DB context resolves to — main context → real ledger, sandbox context → sandbox ledger.
5. The stale comment at `internal/events/commit.go:135-138` (claims sandbox ledger routing that never existed) gets corrected as part of the implementation.

## Per-use-case behavior under the policy

- **Real emits** (main checkout, CLI or hook-attributed): unchanged — real ledger, write-time auto-commit on main.
- **Self-dev worktree session routed to the sandbox**: DB row → sandbox `endless.db`; ledger line → `<sandbox>/db-ledger/`, no commit.
- **`worktree land`**: unchanged (runs in main DB context) — auto-commit globs, orphan-drop, `task.landed` emit to the real ledger.
- **`validate-db` / `rebuild-db`**: follow the resolver; sandbox rebuilds replay only sandbox-born events (the sandbox DB is seeded near-empty, so that is the complete correct history for it).
- **Test harnesses**: unchanged — throwaway `git init` repos with `--config-dir` tempdirs are not sandboxes (not under `sandboxes/`), so they keep real commit behavior.
- **Multi-dev sync**: unaffected — only the real ledger is committed and synced; sandbox ledgers are node-local and disposable.

## History corrected

Sandbox emits landing in the real ledger was never decided. No decision on file says so; the `commit.go` comment asserting sandbox ledger routing was written by a prior agent session and was never true at any point (`writer.go` has derived the ledger root from the registered project path since E-805). Verified empirically: ~35 live sandboxes' node ids match segment files in the real ledger (e-1567: 156 lines, e-1601: 101, e-1541: 97, ...) while zero ledger files exist inside any sandbox. What Mike remembered as deliberate was E-1309 (worktree emits write/commit to main to avoid rebase conflicts — still correct, unchanged) and skip-worktree on `.claude/settings.json` (E-998, unrelated to ledger files).

## Rejected options, with reasons

- **Status quo** (sandbox emits → real ledger): the bug. 41 foreign node ids, ~1,071 lines, ~23% of the real ledger.
- **Worktree-hosted sandbox ledger**, including the `.gitignored` `db-ledger/sandbox/` subdir variant: lives inside a checkout of the real repo, so it is guarded-against rather than structurally unable to ride the land rebase into main; splits the DB from its WAL lifecycle-wise (worktree drop vs sandbox destroy are independent). The subdir variant is functionally the sandbox-dir option with git standing nearby for no reason. Mike concurred after working the variant through.
- **DB-only sandbox emits** (no ledger at all): breaks events-authoritative — a sandbox could never `rebuild-db`, and self-dev sessions would not exercise the write path they are usually developing.
- **Repoint the sandbox's `projects.path` at the sandbox dir**: re-routes with zero Go changes but lies about where the project lives, `path` serves other purposes, and the commit path would hard-fail on a non-repo.
- **`git init` each sandbox** to keep the commit path uniform: commits nobody ever reads; breaks sandbox-is-a-plain-dir; the commit machinery is already exercised by the throwaway-repo harnesses.

## Cleanup of the existing pollution (decides E-1730's approach)

**Excise now, once, as a bug cleanup.** The leaked lines were written by a routing bug and were never legitimate history; delete them from the real segment files in a normal hygiene commit on main (file edit, not git-history rewrite). **Append-only remains the rule for legitimate history going forward.** Tombstoning (E-1716/E-1720) is reserved for events that were real but wrong — its natural home is the multi-dev future. This resolves the E-1730-vs-E-1716 tension: they are different tools for different classes of bad events, not competing answers to the same question.

Constraints on the excision:

- **Per-line classification, not per-node.** Some foreign-node segments interleave real events (`task.landed` for E-1542 and E-1628 sit inside otherwise-junk segments), and sandbox `worktree-e-1507` shares node id `a7f3` with the real node, so its emits hide inside real segments.
- **Ordering (raised by Mike): land the routing fix before excising.** Existing live self-dev worktree sessions run pre-fix binaries and keep writing sandbox emits into the real ledger until E-1729 lands and those sessions end or rebuild. E-1730 is already blocked by E-1729, which encodes the ordering. A second sweep after the fleet turns over catches stragglers.
- **No per-worktree fixing is needed beyond that.** Retained worktrees hold polluted committed copies of the segments, but (a) no read path ever reads a worktree's ledger copy — `validate-db`/`rebuild-db` resolve the registered main-checkout path; (b) branches don't carry ledger commits, so the land rebase replaces a worktree's ledger state with main's excised state for free; (c) dropped worktrees take their copies with them.

## Boundary with E-1665

The routing fix makes sandbox-context pollution impossible by construction. It does NOT cover a hand-run `event emit --project-root <real repo>` from a non-sandbox context — that hazard remains E-1665's scope (safe-by-construction testing of the emit path).

## Follow-ups spawned

- Decision: ledger target follows the active DB context (decides E-1729).
- Decision: excise-once cleanup, append-only protects legitimate history (decides E-1730).
- Task: land-time gate — refuse `worktree land` when the task branch's commits touch `.endless/db-ledger/` (cleans up E-1733).
- E-1729's re-plan is deliberately NOT done here (awaits Mike's go-ahead). Its planner should absorb: the resolver shape, 4-not-3 commit callsites, read symmetry, and the stale-comment fix.

Sandbox DB -> db-ledger/ inside the sandbox dir; never touches git; erased atomically by sandbox destroy. One in-code resolver returns the ledger target (root + commit-or-not) alongside DB-context resolution; all four CommitLedgerSegment callsites and both ProjectToTempDB callsites consume it — no flag, no env var, no config file. Reads are symmetric: validate-db/rebuild-db replay the active context's ledger. payload.title: Refuse worktree land when the task branch's commits touch .endless/db-ledger
payload.description: A commit on a task branch touching .endless/db-ledger/ is always wrong: ledger auto-commits belong to the main checkout only (E-1309), and a branch-side ledger commit rides the land rebase into main. Add a gate to worktree land that refuses when the branch's base..HEAD commits touch .endless/db-ledger/, naming the offending commits loudly. Backstop to ED-1525's routing policy.

payload.title: Ledger edit policy: bug-written lines may be excised; real-but-wrong events are tombstoned
payload.description: The append-only invariant protects legitimate history, not every byte ever appended. Three classes of ledger line, three treatments: (1) Legitimate events are immutable forever; corrections happen by appending new events. (2) Real-but-wrong events — genuine actions recorded with wrong content — are neutralized by appended tombstone/revert entries the projector skips (the E-1716/E-1720 mechanism); mandatory once segments sync across nodes, because another node may already have consumed them. (3) Bug-written garbage — lines a defect wrote into a ledger they were never legitimate history of — may be excised by editing the segment files in a normal hygiene commit; the git history of the mistake is preserved, the ledger's meaning is not rewritten because these lines never carried meaning. Classification between (2) and (3) is per-line, never per-node: node ids can be shared or interleave real events with garbage.

payload.reason: Recorded as an action decision (excise these specific lines, in this order), not architecture. Superseded by ED-1527, which states the enduring policy; the one-time action detail lives in E-1733's outcome and belongs in E-1730's plan.

payload.title: Reject --db in non-self_dev projects instead of silently creating a stray sandbox endless.db
payload.description: --db chooses where endless.db lives; a non-self_dev project has exactly one DB, so the flag is invalid there — reject BOTH values loudly. Today config.apply_db_choice checks only the worktree path shape (no self_dev check), every downstream project's worktrees match it, and db.get_connection then silently mkdirs the sandbox path and creates a fresh empty endless.db in the cache. Full validation matrix and code anchors in analysis.

fields.analysis: Decided validation matrix (Mike, 2026-07-05): project not self_dev -> any --db value is an error, main included (a silent no-op masks confusion about what the flag does). Self_dev project -> --db main valid anywhere in the project (worktrees need it to escape the sandbox; the E-1429 gate requires --db there), --db sandbox additionally requires cwd inside a .endless/worktrees/e-NNN worktree (existing check, keep it). Why the hole exists: the self_dev gates were added piecemeal to other layers — gated_worktree_root (the E-1429 requirement gate), the E-1513 re-exec, and Go's SelfDetectWorktreeSandbox — but the validator config.apply_db_choice never got one; it only asks 'is cwd worktree-shaped'. db.get_connection's ensure_config_dir then creates the missing dir + empty DB on first connect, which is what turns the missing check into silent stray state. The rejection message must be plain (no internal task IDs) and say the flag only applies to projects with self_dev enabled. Scope note: sandboxes as a product concept stay open to ALL projects (project-specific files via hook scripts, separate feature); this bug is strictly about the endless.db location flag.

payload.title: Implement sqlite-vec-backed semantic search (endless search) over tasks and decisions
payload.description: Umbrella for semantic search over the endless ledger using sqlite-vec (in-DB vector KNN). Store an embedding per task/decision (title+description) and answer nearest-neighbor queries sub-millisecond over the 1400+ item ledger, catching paraphrase matches that keyword LIKE misses (e.g. 'Ship endless session id subcommand' vs 'Add endless session id verb'). Powers several consumers: an 'endless search' command, dup-candidate surfacing at task-add time, and relates_to / related-decision suggestions. Open prerequisite Mike is planning: sqlite-vec research — the embedding source must be fast and LOCAL so queries stay sub-second (a network embed adds ~100ms; a full claude -p adds ~10s and is rejected). DB access is being ported to Go (E-1486), so this lands Go-side. Child plans to be filled after the sqlite-vec research. Emerged from the E-1723 brainstorm on search-before-filing.

payload.title: Deny task add on semantic-dup matches; override with --ignore-dups=<count>
payload.description: When 'endless task add' runs, query the sqlite-vec semantic index (E-1738) for existing UNIMPLEMENTED tasks (unplanned/ready/underway/revisit/blocked; skip settled assumed/confirmed/completed/declined/obsolete) similar to the new title+description. If matches exceed the similarity threshold, DENY the add and list them (id, status, title). The agent overrides with --ignore-dups=<num_dups> where the value MUST equal the number of dups found — a bare boolean --ignore-dups is rejected, so Claude cannot habitually bypass the check without reading the findings. Dup detection stays Claude's judgment: semantic similarity surfaces candidates, not verdicts (a research task and its do-it follow-up score similar but are not dups); the count-matching override forces Claude to actually look. Depends on E-1738's sqlite-vec 'endless search' so task-add stays sub-second (no claude -p at file-time). Converts agent-memory lesson search-before-filing.

# E-1648 — Add a submitted status and approve gate to the task status workflow

## Context / governing decisions
This implements an approval gate already decided in pieces:
- **D-1522** (accepted): `ready` = approved-to-spawn, plan optional — a task reaches `ready` via
  an approved plan OR an approved sufficient description.
- **D-1513** (proposed): plan-attach must not auto-promote; a pre-approval state exists (named
  `unapproved` there) before a human `approve` → `ready`.
- **D-1498** (accepted): today drafted-awaiting-approval is encoded as `unplanned` + text present
  (no separate status).
- **D-1499** (accepted): status changes go through the `endless task change` picker of valid
  transitions (no typed status value).

This task **supersedes D-1498's "reuse unplanned+text"** by introducing a distinct pre-approval
status, and **renames D-1513's `unapproved` → `submitted`** (positive/active; pairs with a
`submit` action). Net lifecycle:

    unplanned → submitted → (approve) ready → underway → unverified → confirmed | assumed

`submitted` = spec-complete, agent-set, awaiting approval; reachable two ways — the agent attached
a plan OR judged the description a sufficient spec (plan-vs-no-plan carried by whether `tasks.text`
is populated, not by status). `unplanned` = genuinely needs design. This makes unplanned-vs-submitted
the spawn-readiness signal the agent sets proactively (kills the recurring "is this enough to
spawn?" question).

## Decisions (resolved 2026-07-02 with Mike)
- Pre-approval state is named **`submitted`** (rename of D-1513's `unapproved`).
- **E-1648 owns defining the complete canonical status set** — no prior decision retired `blocked`.
- The workflow gets a **new consolidating decision** (not a finalize-in-place of D-1513).

## Deliverables
1. **Status + verbs.** Add `submitted`; add `submit` (agent-set) and `approve` (human → `ready`)
   verbs. Remove the plan-attach auto-promote (D-1498/D-1513). Forbid `kind=background` sessions
   from `approve` and from picking up non-`ready` work.
2. **Define + enforce the canonical status set.** E-1648 owns this. Working set:
   `unplanned, submitted, ready, underway, unverified, confirmed, assumed, revisit` + terminal
   `completed, obsolete, declined`. **Remove `blocked`** from every code path (e.g. the
   active-status `NOT IN (...)` filter in task_cmd.py) — blocking is carried by the `blocked_by`
   relation, not a status. Confirm `revisit` and the terminal set while sweeping.
3. **Teach every status classifier the set** — actionable / terminal / blocks-dependents / picker
   transitions (D-1499). Status literals live at ~two dozen sites across Go (sessionstatuscmd,
   monitor/task.go, events/executor.go, web/…) and Python (task_cmd.py, db.py, cli.py,
   suggestions_cmd.py); sweep them so none is blind to `submitted` or still treats `blocked` as live.
4. **Mermaid workflow chart.** A single `stateDiagram` of the full lifecycle, embedded in README.md,
   CLAUDE.md, and endless guide from one canonical source. Renders from the deliverable-5 decision.
5. **New consolidating decision** (`endless decision add`): "Canonical task status workflow" —
   references and supersedes D-1522, D-1513, D-1498, D-1499. Records the full valid status set
   (deliverable 2) and every legal transition. Single source of truth the mermaid renders from.

## Verification
- `endless task submit` / `approve` round-trip in a sandbox DB: unplanned → submit → submitted →
  approve → ready; a background session is rejected from `approve`.
- Grep confirms no classifier still treats a removed status (`blocked`) as live; the mermaid
  renders in all three docs from the single source.



## On completion (memory prune)
Once this ships, prune the converted agent-memory files feedback_plan_attach_promotes_to_ready.md and feedback_proactive_spawn_readiness.md + their MEMORY.md index lines — the lessons now live in the submitted/approve gate (per E-1723).

Sandboxes are a general product concept (any project may get one holding project files via hooks); only the endless.db location decides ledger routing. (2) --db flag validity is being tightened separately by the related bug fix (self_dev-only, both values); this task's resolver simply inherits whatever DB context resolution produces. (3) There are FOUR CommitLedgerSegment callsites (the epic-derivation emitter is the fourth), not the three this task's drafted text says. (5) Fix the stale comment at internal/events/commit.go ensureMainCheckout claiming sandbox ledger routing exists. Rationale/alternatives: ED-1525 and E-1733's outcome.

shape for the **high-value (a) feature** shortlist one candidate at a time, filed
(or folded) the follow-ups, and set up the structure to finish the med-(a) and
(b)-guide tails in separate sessions. A cross-cutting memory-hygiene principle also
emerged and reshaped what "conversion" means here.

## Governing principle (emerged this session)
Once a **deterministic gate** (a hook/validator the agent cannot bypass) ships a
lesson, the paired agent-memory is **redundant and gets pruned** — belt & suspenders
is explicitly not wanted. Memory earns its keep only while the product does *not* yet
enforce the lesson (stopgap until the fix ships) or for lessons with no product
surface at all. Recorded in `feedback_endless_fixes_ship_in_product_not_my_memory`
(corrected — it previously said "keep as reinforcement on top"). Consequence: every
conversion task carries a "prune the memory on land" note, and lessons already fully
gated were pruned now.

## High-value (a) dispositions (6 clusters)

1. **`never-discard-auto-record-commits`** → filed **E-1734** (next).

   worktree-removal paths refuse uncommitted work: `worktree drop` refuses
   dirty/unmerged/foreign without --force; `worktree land` guards unmanaged dirt

   E-1415 loss predates all three. Memory obsolete — Mike pruned it.

4. **plan-path gate** (`no-plan-files-in-main` + `plan-files-via-task-update`)

   `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` (main *and* worktree mirror), routing to

5. **status state-machine** (`plan-attach-promotes-to-ready` +

   E-1648 is both lessons verbatim: unplanned → submitted → (approve) ready; remove

6. **`search-before-filing`** → filed **E-1738** (sqlite-vec semantic-search epic,

  status set") and "remove `blocked` from every code path" now belong SOLELY to

# E-1532 — Formalize task phases & statuses via FK to values tables — PLAN

Decisions locked 2026-06-23 (rev. 2026-06-24). **Blocked by E-1252** (status
renames): the seed must use E-1252's final names, so that decision lands first.

## Locked decisions
1. **One task.** Phases + statuses values tables, dropping `blocked`, the 9-row
   cleanup, and collapsing the duplicated validation — all here, not split.
2. **Blocked by E-1252.** Final status slugs come from the rename decision; the
   seed (and the one-time row rename) reflect its outcome.
3. **Drop `blocked` as a stored status** — not seeded. Blocking is derived from the
   `blocked_by` relation + blocker status (`endless guide tasks`); a stored value
   only duplicates it and goes stale (it bit E-1621) and carries no "why" (row 627
   proved the reason is unrecoverable without a relation). Removing it also
   dissolves the "what status on unblock?" problem — the real work-state is never
   overwritten.
4. **Enforcement = a real DB-level FK, by SLUG, done now (not deferred).** Keep
   `tasks.status`/`.phase` as TEXT and add `FOREIGN KEY(status) REFERENCES
   task_statuses(slug)` and `FOREIGN KEY(phase) REFERENCES task_phases(slug)`. The
   DB then rejects any invalid value on *every* write path (Go executor, raw SQL,
   Python), and the TEXT column means **no call-site churn** — every reader/writer
   keeps treating status/phase as the same string.
5. **Phase values** = the in-use five: `urgent, now, next, later, maybe`.
6. **Status values** = current set minus `blocked`, with E-1252 renames applied:
   (`needs_plan`→?, `in_progress`→?), `ready, verify, confirmed, assumed, completed,
   revisit, declined, obsolete`.

## Migration mechanics (the FK on existing columns)
SQLite can't ALTER-add a constraint, so the `.go` change-file (run with
`foreign_keys` OFF — the runner's default, per E-1571) does a standard `tasks`
table-rebuild:
1. create+seed `task_phases` / `task_statuses`;
2. run the 9-row cleanup (below) so no row holds a soon-invalid value;
3. `CREATE TABLE tasks_new (… same columns …, FOREIGN KEY(status) REFERENCES
   task_statuses(slug), FOREIGN KEY(phase) REFERENCES task_phases(slug), + existing
   self/other FKs)`;
4. `INSERT INTO tasks_new SELECT * FROM tasks` (ids preserved → 8 inbound-FK tables
   stay valid under FK-off);
5. `DROP TABLE tasks; ALTER TABLE tasks_new RENAME TO tasks`;
6. recreate the `tasks_updated_at` trigger and indexes (`idx_session_tasks_task`,
   `idx_project_next_tasks_task`);
7. `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` before the runner re-enables FKs.
`schema.sql` declares the post-state (the two tables + FK clauses on the `tasks`
CREATE) for fresh/sandbox DBs.

## Steps
1. **schema.sql** — add `task_phases(id, slug UNIQUE NOT NULL, label NOT NULL)` and
   `task_statuses(...)` with idempotent `INSERT OR IGNORE` seeds; add the two FK
   clauses to the `tasks` CREATE.
2. **`.go` change-file** — the rebuild above, against the populated real DB.
3. **Collapse validation to one source** — replace `cli.py:121 TASK_STATUSES` and
   the inline tuple in `task_cmd.py:3267` (and the phase choices) with a lookup of
   the seeded slugs; `click.Choice`/`MultiChoice` build from that single source.
   (The DB FK is the backstop; this keeps the friendly CLI error.)
4. **9-row cleanup** (re-verify the set at implementation time), inside the
   change-file before the rebuild:
   - 627 → `obsolete` (superseded by E-891).
   - 496, 520, 581, 616, 624, 634, 721, 1515 → `ready` if the row has non-empty
     text, else `needs_plan`; leave their `blocked_by` relations intact.
   One-time ledger hygiene (not shipped migration code).
5. **Apply E-1252 renames** — same change-file: `UPDATE tasks SET status=<new>` for
   each renamed slug, seed the table with new slugs, sweep code/docs/guide/handoff
   references off the old strings.
6. **Tests** — DB rejects an unseeded status (incl. `blocked`) and a bad phase;
   accepts each seeded one; cleanup leaves zero `blocked` rows; the rebuild
   preserved inbound FKs (`foreign_key_check` clean).

## Out of scope
- The rename strings themselves — decided by E-1252 (this task's blocker).



## Scope note (E-1723, 2026-07-05) — sole owner of the status-set definition
E-1648 was decoupled from this task (no longer blocked here); it ships the approval
gate on the current free-TEXT column and adds `submitted` as a plain value.

  stored `blocked` (Deliverable/step list above). E-1648 no longer claims these.

  set (with E-1252's landed renames: `unplanned`/`underway`/`unverified`) at
  implementation time, and confirm `submitted` is present and `blocked` absent.

# E-1202 — Block direct Write/Edit of plan files — PLAN

## Mechanism
A new preToolUse gate in `internal/hookcmd/claude.go` refuses any
Write/Edit/NotebookEdit whose target is a task plan file `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md`,
redirecting to `endless task update --text`. The CLI's own materialization
(`_materialize_plan_file` / `_commit_plan_file`, worktree_cmd.py) is untouched — it
is not a Claude tool call, so the hook never sees it; the land-produces-plan-markdown
flow is intact.

## Path pattern (resolved)
`planFileRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(^|/)\.endless/plans/E-\d+\.md$`)`
- Matches absolute (`…/.endless/plans/E-1202.md`) and repo-relative paths.
- Anchored `$`; requires `E-<digits>.md` immediately after `plans/`, so it EXCLUDES
  any subdirectory (e.g. a future `.endless/plans/snapshots/…`) and any non-plan file
  in the dir. Current layout is flat `E-NNN.md`; no snapshots subdir exists — verified.
- Does NOT touch Claude's plan-mode `plan.md` (different path + flow).

## Scope (resolved)
Fires for BOTH main and worktree targets — plan files must never be hand-written
anywhere; only `task update --text` writes them. Independent of tracking_mode (like
the worktree and commit-on-main gates).

## Changes
1. Add package var `planFileRe` and `blockPlanFileWriteIfApplicable(payload)` —
   model on `blockCommitOnMainIfApplicable`: `extractFilePath` -> regex test ->
   `blockToolUse(msg)`. Reuses existing `writeTools` / `extractFilePath`.
2. Call it in `handlePreToolUse`, in the write-tool section: AFTER the
   `if !writeTools[payload.ToolName] { return nil }` early-return and BEFORE the
   `enforceWorktreeGate` call, so a plan-file write in main gets the plan-specific
   message rather than the generic worktree refusal.
3. Block message (NO internal task IDs, per the user-facing-string rule):
   "BLOCKED: refusing a direct Write/Edit of a task plan file
   (.endless/plans/E-NNN.md). Plan content lives in tasks.text (the source of truth);
   the file is a mirror endless writes and commits for you. Editing it directly leaves
   the DB stale, and if the worktree is later dropped the edit is silently lost.
   Author the plan at a temp path, then run:
     endless task update <id> --text <path>
   Never hand-edit or git-commit the plan file yourself."

## Verification
`tests/tasks/e-1202-verify.sh` (committed; shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`).
The gate is pure path-matching (no DB), so drive the worktree hook binary with
synthetic PreToolUse payloads:
- Write to `<abs>/.endless/plans/E-999.md` -> REFUSED (exit 2; message names
  `task update --text`).
- Write to `<abs>/.endless/plans/snapshots/E-999.md` -> ALLOWED (subdir excluded).
- Write to `<abs>/.endless/plans/notes.md` and a normal source file -> ALLOWED.
- Edit and NotebookEdit variants of the plan-file path -> REFUSED.
- Sanity: `endless task update <id> --text <file>` still materializes the mirror.
Handoff: `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1202-verify.sh`.

# E-1736 — Refuse worktree land when the branch's commits touch `.endless/db-ledger/`

## Context

`.endless/db-ledger/` is the write-ahead log for Endless's SQLite DB — its JSONL
segments ARE the database (corrupting them corrupts the DB). Ledger auto-commits
are recorded on the **main checkout only** (the ED-1525 routing policy, enforced
in Go at `internal/events/commit.go`'s `ensureMainCheckout`). A ledger commit on
a *task branch* is therefore always wrong: it rides the land rebase straight into
`main`, injecting a branch-authored ledger segment into shared history.

Today, `endless worktree land` only catches this *indirectly* — if the branch-side
ledger commit happens to conflict during the Step 4 rebase, the user sees a generic
rebase-failure message. A ledger commit that rebases cleanly slips into `main`
silently. This task adds a **deterministic gate**: before the rebase, refuse the
land outright when any surviving branch commit touches the ledger dir, naming the
offending commits. It's a backstop to the ED-1525 routing policy — the Go guard
prevents these commits from being *created*; this gate stops any that slip through
from *landing*.

**Key subtlety (from E-1733's planning input):** a naive "does `base..HEAD` touch
`.endless/db-ledger/`" check FALSE-POSITIVES on normal lands. Branches routinely
fork from `main` while its tip is the rolling *"Endless: record ledger entry"*
commit; when `main` later amends that tip, the branch's fork-point copy becomes an
orphan reachable from the branch but not `main` — it appears in `base..HEAD` and
touches the ledger by definition. Land's **Step 3.7** (`_drop_orphan_amendable_commits`,
E-1342) already silently drops exactly that class. The gate therefore runs **after
Step 3.7** and refuses only what survives — Step 3.7 remains the sole authority on
legitimately-discardable ledger commits; the gate does not re-implement its logic.

## Files

- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — add the constant, the helper, and the gate.
- `tests/test_worktree_land_dbledger_gate.py` — new pytest for the helper (mirrors
  `tests/test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`).
- `tests/tasks/e-1736-verify.sh` — new isolated verify script (mandated).

## Implementation

### 1. Ledger-path constant

Near `AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS` (`worktree_cmd.py:54`), add a single source of truth for
the ledger dir pathspec (Python has none today — only the `*.jsonl` glob):

```python
# E-1736: the DB ledger directory, as a git pathspec. A commit under here
# on a task branch violates the ledger routing policy (ledger entries are
# recorded on the main checkout only) and must never ride a land into main.
DB_LEDGER_DIR = ".endless/db-ledger"
```

### 2. Helper — enumerate surviving ledger-touching commits

Add alongside `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits` (same file, same `_git_run` idiom).
Restrict `git log` by pathspec so it returns *only* commits that touched the ledger
dir — no per-commit `show` walk needed:

```python
def _ledger_touching_commits(
    worktree_path: Path, base_branch: str
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return (sha, subject) for every commit in base..HEAD that modifies a
    file under the DB ledger dir. Empty list when none.

    Backstop to the ledger routing policy: ledger entries are auto-committed
    on the main checkout only, so a branch-side commit under DB_LEDGER_DIR is
    always wrong and would be rebased into main by land. Intended to run AFTER
    Step 3.7's orphan-drop, so legitimately-orphaned base ledger commits are
    already gone and only genuine offenders remain.
    """
    out = _git_run(
        ["log", "--reverse", "--format=%H %s",
         f"{base_branch}..HEAD", "--", DB_LEDGER_DIR],
        cwd=worktree_path,
    )
    commits: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for ln in out.stdout.splitlines():
        if not ln.strip():
            continue
        sha, _, subject = ln.partition(" ")
        commits.append((sha, subject))
    return commits
```

### 3. The gate — new Step 3.75, after 3.7, before 3.8

Insert between the Step 3.7 advisory echo (`worktree_cmd.py:1614`) and Step 3.8's
`_guard_dirty_worktree` (`:1616`). Refusal message names each offending commit, is
plain-language, and cites **no internal task IDs** (per house rule on user-facing
strings):

```python
        # Step 3.75 (backstop to the ledger routing policy): refuse if any
        # commit surviving Step 3.7 still touches the DB ledger. Step 3.7
        # already dropped the legitimately-orphaned base ledger commits;
        # anything still under DB_LEDGER_DIR is a genuine branch-side ledger
        # commit that would be rebased into main and corrupt shared history.
        offenders = _ledger_touching_commits(worktree_path, base_branch)
        if offenders:
            noun = "commit" if len(offenders) == 1 else "commits"
            listing = "\n".join(
                f"  {sha[:12]}  {subject}" for sha, subject in offenders
            )
            raise click.ClickException(
                f"cannot land {canonical}: the branch has {len(offenders)} "
                f"{noun} modifying the database ledger ({DB_LEDGER_DIR}/):\n\n"
                f"{listing}\n\n"
                f"Ledger entries are recorded on the main checkout, never on a "
                f"task branch — landing these would rebase a branch-authored "
                f"ledger segment into main and corrupt the shared database "
                f"history. Remove these commits from the branch before retrying "
                f"(inspect each with `git show <sha>`)."
            )
```

Step 4's existing rebase-failure message (which still mentions "db-ledger entry
or config.json") stays as a fallback for the config.json / genuine-conflict cases
— no change needed there.

## Why this shape

- **After Step 3.7, restricted by pathspec** — avoids the orphan false-positive
  without duplicating Step 3.7's exclusion logic; Step 3.7 stays the single
  authority on discardable ledger commits.
- **`git log … -- <pathspec>`** — one call returns exactly the offenders; no
  per-commit `show --name-only` walk.
- **Deterministic, pre-rebase** — closes the silent-clean-rebase hole that Step 4's
  conflict-only message misses.

## Testing

### pytest — `tests/test_worktree_land_dbledger_gate.py`

Mirror `test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`'s real-git-repo fixtures
(`repo_with_worktree`, `_create_task_branch`, `_commit`, `_amend_with_extra_line`).
Cover the helper directly:

1. **Clean branch → no offenders.** User commit only; `_ledger_touching_commits`
   returns `[]`.
2. **Standalone branch-side ledger commit → 1 offender.** Commit touching
   `.endless/db-ledger/x.jsonl` on the branch; returns 1 (sha, subject).
3. **Orphan false-positive → no offenders after Step 3.7.** Branch forks at an old
   ledger tip, `main` amends it (the E-1342 scenario). Run
   `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits` first (as land does), THEN
   `_ledger_touching_commits` — must return `[]`. This is the critical regression.
4. **Mid-branch ledger commit Step 3.7 won't drop → caught by gate.** User commit,
   then a ledger commit on top. Step 3.7 breaks at the user commit (drops nothing);
   the gate returns 1 offender.

### Verify script — `tests/tasks/e-1736-verify.sh`

Fully isolated throwaway repos (the E-1729 harness shape: `mktemp -d`, real
`git init` main + `git worktree add` branch, cleanup on exit; colored pass/fail
+ summary; exit 0 all-passed / 1 any-fail / 2 setup error). Full end-to-end
`endless worktree land` can't be exercised in isolation — `land_worktree` opens
with `config.default_db_to_main()` and resolves the *real* project root — so the
script drives the gate at the code-path level via `uv run python -c` importing
`_ledger_touching_commits` (and `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits` for the orphan
case), against the four scenarios above. It also runs the new pytest and the
existing `test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py` as a no-regression check.

Handoff to Mike is exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1736-verify.sh
```

## Out of scope / not doing

- No change to the Go event layer (E-1309 already guards *creation*; this guards
  *landing*).
- No rewrite of Step 4's fallback message.
- No auto-remediation of offending commits — the gate refuses and instructs; it
  does not rewrite the user's branch.

## Completion

- `endless task update E-1736 --status unverified --db main`.
- Report git/worktree side-effects + the return line; do not self-confirm.
