- `internal/monitor/session_status.go` also references `⁇`. Check whether it renders its own legend needing the same treatment, or shares this path — keep scope to the `sessionstatuscmd` list view unless they share the legend.

## Out of scope

- The stale-binary symptom where `submitted` tasks render `⁇` instead of `▶` — that's fixed by rebuilding the binary (`just install` / worktree `just build`), not a code change here.

## Verify

Deliver `tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh` (model it on `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`:
pass/fail per check, `ALL PASSED` summary, exit 0 all-pass / 1 any-fail / 2 setup).
The verify-handoff to Mike must present **only**:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh

Fold every check into that script; do NOT hand Mike a manual checklist. Exercise the
renderer headlessly via the `--task` / `--from-session` / `--cols` flags (no tmux
needed) against representative row sets, asserting:

- A view with only do/plan rows → legend lists just those glyphs (no orphan/verify/
  other/blocked/blocks/dirty entries).
- A view containing a landed (or otherwise `actOther`) row → legend includes `⁇` and
  its label.
- A view with a blocked row → `⊗ blocked`; with a blocking row → `⏸ blocks`; with a
  dirty (worktree-diverged) row → `◆ dirty`. Each absent when no such row exists.
- The legend contains **no `|`** separator.
- **Parity:** one `session status` frame is byte-identical to one `session monitor`
  frame for the same rows.

This feature is fully headless-verifiable — no manual step is expected.

# E-1734 — Block agent git ops that discard db-ledger commits — PLAN

## Mechanism
New preToolUse Bash gate `blockLedgerDiscardIfApplicable(payload)` in
`internal/hookcmd/claude.go`, called from `handlePreToolUse`'s Bash branch alongside
`blockCommitOnMainIfApplicable` / `blockSqliteAgainstEndlessIfApplicable`. It runs
only when the command matches a covered destructive verb (regex-gate FIRST, so
ordinary Bash pays no cost); on a match it resolves the commit range that verb would
discard and blocks IFF any commit in that range touched the DB WAL at
`.endless/db-ledger/`. Git is run via `exec.Command` from `payload.CWD`, modeled on
`isInMainCheckout` / `isInActiveMerge`.

## Ledger-commit detection (unifying, robust)
A range "contains a ledger commit" iff this is non-empty:
    git -C <cwd> log <range> --format=%H -- .endless/db-ledger/
Path-based, so it catches BOTH ledger commits (`Endless: record ledger entry`,
`events/commit.go` `LedgerCommitSubject`) and auto-record commits (`Endless:
auto-record session activity`) — both touch `.endless/db-ledger/` — and is robust to
subject wording. (db-ledger is the DB WAL; losing it corrupts the DB.)

## Covered verbs + range resolution
1. `git reset --hard <target>` (SURGICAL) — discarded range = `<target>..HEAD`. Parse
   `<target>` from the command. Bare `git reset --hard` (or target == HEAD) discards
   no commits -> allow. Block iff `<target>..HEAD` touches db-ledger.
2. `git branch -D <branch>` (SURGICAL) — discarded = commits reachable from `<branch>`
   but no other ref. Detect via `git log <branch> --not <all-other-refs> --format=%H
   -- .endless/db-ledger/` (build the exclude set from `git for-each-ref` minus
   `<branch>`). Block iff non-empty. (`-d` is safe-delete; git already refuses
   unmerged — still gate `-D`, and `branch --delete --force`.)
3. `git push --force` / `--force-with-lease` / `-f` (BEST-EFFORT) — discarded =
   commits on the remote-tracking ref not in the pushed tip:
   `git log <pushed-tip>..<remote>/<branch> --format=%H -- .endless/db-ledger/`.
   Uses the LOCAL remote-tracking ref, which may be stale without a fetch -> BEST
   EFFORT; the block message says so. Reliable resolution is the maybe/brainstorm.

## Out of scope (this task)
- Interactive rebase (`rebase -i`) — drop set lives in the interactive todo, not the
  command; also blocked in this harness.
- Non-interactive `rebase --onto` / `filter-branch` / other rewrites — share
  force-push's static-resolution difficulty; folded into the same maybe/brainstorm.

## Placement + block/allow discipline
- Call in the `handlePreToolUse` Bash branch, after `blockCommitOnMainIfApplicable`.
- On no verb match / empty range / any git error -> return silently (ALLOW). NEVER
  block on detection failure: a false block on a benign op trains bypass, defeating
  the gate. Surgical means block ONLY on a positive db-ledger hit.
- Block message: list the offending commit(s) (short `%h %s`), state they carry the
  DB WAL (`.endless/db-ledger/`) so discarding corrupts the DB, and give the safe
  path: `git revert` the specific bad commits, or pick a reset/branch target at or
  above the ledger commit. NO internal task IDs (user-facing-string rule). For
  force-push, add the best-effort caveat (remote-tracking ref may be stale; fetch
  first).

## New regexes (package vars)
`gitResetHardRe`, `gitBranchDeleteRe`, `gitForcePushRe` — anchored like `gitCommitRe`
(`^\s*git\s+...`), tolerant of leading whitespace and flag ordering.

## Verification
`tests/tasks/e-1734-verify.sh` (committed; shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`).
In an ISOLATED temp git repo (never the real DB/ledger — see isolate-hook-verification),
seed commits mixing normal changes with a commit touching `.endless/db-ledger/seg.jsonl`:
- `reset --hard` to BELOW the ledger commit -> REFUSED; to a target ABOVE it (no
  ledger in range) -> ALLOWED; bare `git reset --hard` -> ALLOWED.
- `branch -D` of a branch whose unique commits touch db-ledger -> REFUSED; of a
  merged / no-ledger branch -> ALLOWED.
- `push --force` best-effort: with a local bare repo as "remote" whose tracking ref
  holds a ledger commit not in the pushed tip -> REFUSED.
- git error / non-git dir / unrelated Bash -> ALLOWED (no false block).
Handoff: `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1734-verify.sh`.

payload.title: Decide how to reliably detect ledger commits discarded by force-push and history rewrites
payload.description: Force-push and other history rewrites (non-interactive rebase --onto, filter-branch) do not expose their discarded commit set in the command the way reset --hard / branch -D do — the drop set depends on remote-tracking state (possibly stale without a fetch) or a computed rebase plan. E-1734 ships SURGICAL db-ledger-discard detection for reset --hard + branch -D plus a BEST-EFFORT remote-tracking check for force-push. This brainstorm decides how to resolve the hard cases reliably: e.g. require/trigger a fresh fetch before judging force-push, install a git pre-push hook, resolve the rewrite's drop set, or accept best-effort + a loud warn. Emerged from E-1734's scoping. Endless-scoped.

fields.description: The worktree reaper logs 'removed <dir>' for stranded orphan worktree dirs (non-empty, no .git, untracked by git) on every sweep, yet never deletes them: 'git worktree remove' fails with 'is not a working tree', the os.Remove fallback refuses the non-empty dir, its error is discarded, and the function returns reaped=true anyway — so the log lies and the dirs persist forever. Fix: auto-remove stranded orphans via a strictly path-scoped RemoveAll (only <main>/.endless/worktrees/e-NNN, non-symlink) and surface genuine removal failures instead of faking success.

fields.text:
# Fix worktree reaper: stranded orphan dirs falsely logged "removed", never deleted — PLAN

## Context

The self-dev worktree reaper (`ReapWorktreesForProject` → `ReapStaleWorktrees` →
`maybeReapWorktree` in `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`; reaper origin E-1337)
logs `reap worktrees: removed <dir>` for the SAME orphaned dirs on every sweep
(observed on each land: e-1281, e-1381, e-1416) — yet the dirs persist.

Root cause (fully traced): those dirs are orphaned leftovers — non-empty, NO
`.git`, and absent from `git worktree list` (a prior reap or `git worktree prune`
dropped the git admin record but left the files). The flow:

1. Conditions 4 & 5 run `git -C <dir> rev-list main..HEAD --count` and
   `git -C <dir> status --porcelain`. With no `.git` in the dir, git walks UP to
   the main repo: rev-list → 0 (HEAD is main), and `.endless/worktrees/` is
   gitignored so porcelain is empty. Both "pass" — but they validated MAIN, not
   the orphan's contents.
2. `git worktree remove --force <dir>` → `fatal: '…' is not a working tree`
   (exit 128).
3. The `strings.Contains(out, "is not a working tree")` branch runs
   `_ = os.Remove(dir); return true, nil`. `os.Remove` refuses the NON-EMPTY dir,
   the error is discarded, and the function returns `true` anyway → the outer
   sweep logs `removed <dir>` though nothing was removed. Next sweep: identical,
   forever.

Two defects: (a) false success + misleading repeated log; (b) non-empty orphans
are never actually reaped.

## Decision (Mike)

Auto-deleting stranded orphan dirs is the intended behavior — forcing manual
cleanup is not wanted. There is no legitimate case to RETAIN a stranded
(untracked), TTL-expired, no-live-process, already-landed worktree dir: it is
already outside git's management (cannot be committed/landed from), abandoned past
`worktree_ttl`, and its task's deliverable is already on main. So: auto-remove
them, and surface only GENUINE removal errors (e.g. permission denied).

## Changes — `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go`

### 1. Auto-remove the stranded orphan (replace the discarded `os.Remove`)
In `maybeReapWorktree`, the `is not a working tree` branch becomes:
```go
if strings.Contains(out, "is not a working tree") {
    // Orphaned leftover: git no longer tracks it as a worktree (a prior
    // reap/prune dropped the record but left files). Remove the whole dir,
    // strictly path-scoped so RemoveAll can never over-reach. A real failure
    // (permissions, etc.) propagates as an error and is surfaced by the outer
    // sweep's existing log line — no more false "removed".
    if rerr := removeStrandedWorktreeDir(projectRoot, dir); rerr != nil {
        return false, fmt.Errorf("remove stranded worktree dir: %w", rerr)
    }
    return true, nil
}
```

### 2. New guarded remover — `removeStrandedWorktreeDir(projectRoot, dir string) error`
`os.RemoveAll(dir)` ONLY after asserting ALL of:
- `dir` is lexically within `filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".endless", "worktrees")`
  (`filepath.Rel` yields no leading `..` and is not `.`).
- `filepath.Base(dir)` matches `worktreeDirRe` (`e-\d+`).
- `dir` is not a symlink (`os.Lstat` → `mode&os.ModeSymlink == 0`).
Any assertion failing → return an error (never RemoveAll a path we can't vouch
for). This bounds the destructive op to exactly a `<main>/.endless/worktrees/e-NNN`
directory and refuses to follow a symlink to somewhere else.

### 3. Honest reporting
`return true` now means "the dir is actually gone." The tracked-worktree path
(successful `git worktree remove`) is unchanged. Genuine `RemoveAll` failures
propagate as errors → the outer loop's existing
`log.Printf("reap worktrees: %s: %v", …)` surfaces them (once per sweep) instead
of a false "removed".

## Tests — `internal/monitor/reap_worktrees_test.go` (extend existing)
The reaper already exposes test seams (`runGit`, `hasLiveProcessInDir` are
swappable package vars). Add:
- **Stranded-orphan reaped**: a real temp dir, non-empty, no `.git`, under a fake
  `<projectRoot>/.endless/worktrees/e-NNN`; stub `runGit` so `worktree remove`
  returns `fatal: … is not a working tree` and conditions 4/5 pass → assert the
  dir is gone afterward and the call returns reaped=true.
- **Path-guard rejections** for `removeStrandedWorktreeDir`: a dir outside the
  worktrees root, a non-`e-NNN` basename, and a symlink whose target is a
  sentinel dir → assert it returns an error AND the sentinel/target still exists.
- **Empty-orphan regression**: an empty stranded dir is still removed.

## Deliverable — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

The implementing session GENERATES `tests/tasks/e-1745-verify.sh` (self-contained,
shape/output per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`, "ALL PASSED" or a failure list)
and commits it with the implementation. It must:
- `just build` (this is Go), then `go test ./internal/monitor/ -run Reap` → passes.
- Drive `removeStrandedWorktreeDir` behavior with real temp dirs (the reaper's
  `runGit` / `hasLiveProcessInDir` seams are swappable): a non-empty stranded dir
  is removed and reported reaped=true; an empty stranded dir is removed; the path
  guard REFUSES (returns error, deletes nothing) for a dir outside the worktrees
  root, a non-`e-NNN` basename, and a symlink whose target is a sentinel.
- Assert the false-"removed" bug is gone: a removal failure reports an error, not
  a bogus "removed".

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1745-verify.sh
```

MANUAL (the one thing the script can't safely do, since it mutates real dirs):
with the actual stranded dirs (e-1281/e-1381/e-1416) present in the main checkout,
run `endless-go event reap-worktrees` and confirm they are truly deleted and the
"removed" line prints once each, then never again.

## Notes
- The clean/unmerged git checks (conditions 4 & 5) are meaningless for stranded
  dirs (they inspect main). Safety for the auto-delete rests on: task-landed +
  past-TTL + no-live-process + the strict path scope above.

# Version-control all multiline content as committed mirror files — PLAN

## Context

Today only a task's plan (`tasks.text`) is mirrored to a version-controlled file
`.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` (materialized + committed by `worktree_cmd.py`:
`_materialize_plan_file` / `_commit_plan_file_in_worktree`, per the E-1445/E-1525
machinery, ridden to main by worktree-land). Every OTHER multiline field —
`tasks.outcome`, `tasks.analysis`, `tasks.description`, decision bodies — lives
only in the DB. If the DB row is lost or an authoring scratch file is referenced
instead of embedded (the corruption class E-1744 addresses), that content has no
git-backed copy to recover from.

This is the **durability belt** (belt-and-suspenders with the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp`
task): even when content did make it into the DB, it should also exist as a
committed file so a human reviewing the repo on GitHub sees it and it survives a
dropped worktree / lost DB row.

## Approach

Generalize the existing plan-mirror path so it materializes+commits **every**
mirrored multiline field, not just `text`. For now, one subdir per field kind off
`.endless/` (Mike's steer — consolidate the naming convention later):
- `tasks.text`     → `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md`      (existing)
- `tasks.outcome`  → `.endless/outcomes/E-NNN.md`   (new)
- decision bodies  → `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` (new)
- (extend to `analysis`/`description` if the same rule applies — confirm the field
  set at implementation; keep the mechanism field-driven, not copy-pasted.)

### Mechanism (reuse, don't fork)
- Extract the plan-mirror materialize/commit into a small field-agnostic helper:
  given (task/decision id, subdir, content), write `<worktree>/.endless/<subdir>/
  <ID>.md` and stage+commit it. `_materialize_plan_file` becomes one caller.
- Call it from the same CLI write paths that already set these fields
  (`update_plan`, `add_item`, `task complete/assume/replace`, `decision add`) —
  wherever the field's content is written to the DB, also mirror it, exactly as
  `text` is mirrored now.
- Only mirrors when a worktree exists (same as today: no worktree → DB-only, the
  file is born when the worktree is created at claim/spawn). Extend
  `create_task_worktree`'s birth-time materialization to seed ALL field mirrors,
  not just the plan.
- `.gitignore`: none needed — these dirs are tracked content (like `.endless/plans`).

## Open questions (resolve in chat / at implementation)
- Exact field set to mirror (definitely `outcome`; likely `decisions`; confirm
  `analysis`/`description`).
- Decision ID namespace on disk (`ED-NNN.md`) — confirm the prefix matches the CLI.
- Whether to backfill existing rows' mirrors in this task or leave backfill to the
  E-1744 repair pass (recommend: birth-time + write-time here; backfill is a
  one-shot follow-up).

## Deliverable — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

The implementing session GENERATES `tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh` (self-contained,
sandbox DB, shape/output per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`) and commits it with
the implementation. It must cover:
- Set an outcome via `endless task update/complete <id> --outcome "..."` on a task
  WITH a worktree → `.endless/outcomes/E-NNN.md` is written AND committed with the
  content.
- `--outcome-file <f>` → same mirror content.
- Decision body → `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` written+committed.
- Regression: the existing `tasks.text` → `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` mirror still
  works unchanged.
- A task with no worktree → DB-only, no file written (no crash).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh
```

MANUAL (only if it can't be scripted cleanly in the sandbox): land a worktree and
confirm the outcome/decision mirrors arrive on `main` alongside the plan mirror,
and that a fresh claim/spawn seeds the mirrors at worktree birth.

## Notes
- Complements E-1744 (prevents path-corruption + repairs data) and the
  `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task (sanctioned scratch dir). Together: content is
  captured in the DB (source of truth), mirrored to git (this task), authored in a
  co-located non-ephemeral scratch dir, and protected by the flag gate.

# Replace /tmp with project-local .endless/tmp for scratch content — PLAN

## Context

Guides, docs, MEMORY, and spawn-prompt templates tell agents to author content at
a `/tmp/...` path, then load it (`endless task update <id> --text-file <path>`).
`/tmp` is system-global and ephemeral: if content is written there and only
*referenced* from the endless DB (the corruption class E-1744 addresses), or the
worktree is dropped before the content is loaded, it is lost to the ether — and
`/tmp` is wiped on reboot, off in a system dir no one thinks to check.

Fix: sanction a **project-local** scratch dir `.endless/tmp` and recommend it
everywhere `/tmp` is currently recommended. Co-located with the work, survives
reboot, and easy to find if content needs recovering before a worktree is dropped.

This is the **suspenders** (belt-and-suspenders with the multiline-mirror task):
mirrors preserve content that reached the DB; `.endless/tmp` keeps a
forgotten-but-not-yet-loaded scratch file recoverable instead of vaporized. Mike
wants both layers so a single forgotten step never loses important content.

## Changes

### 1. Gitignore
Add `.endless/tmp/` to the repo `.gitignore` (scratch, not tracked content — unlike
`.endless/plans/` and the new `.endless/outcomes/`). Confirm it does not shadow any
tracked `.endless/` path.

### 2. Docs / guides / MEMORY / prompt sweep
`grep` for `/tmp` recommendations and rewrite to `.endless/tmp`:
- `endless guide` source + `docs/guide*` markdown.
- Spawn-prompt templates (the handoff prompts that say "Author the plan at a temp
  path").
- Any `CLAUDE.md` / project-rules snippets.
- The E-1202 hook block message and the E-1744 gate/lint messages say "author at a
  temp path" — point them at `.endless/tmp`.
- User MEMORY entries that recommend `/tmp` (memory is reinforcement; the shipped
  guides/prompts are the real fix).

Be surgical: only rewrite `/tmp` uses that are **scratch-for-endless-content**
recommendations. Leave unrelated `/tmp` references (e.g. genuine OS-temp examples,
test fixtures that must use the system temp) alone — enumerate each hit and judge.

### 3. Ensure the dir exists when recommended
`.endless/tmp` must exist (or be created on demand) so the recommendation isn't a
"no such directory" trap. Options (pick at implementation): create it in the
worktree bootstrap (`post-worktree-create.sh` / `create_task_worktree`), or have
the guide instruct `mkdir -p .endless/tmp`. Prefer bootstrap creation so agents
never hit a missing dir.

## Deliverable — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

The implementing session GENERATES `tests/tasks/e-1748-verify.sh` (self-contained,
shape/output per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`) and commits it with the
implementation. It must assert:
- `.endless/tmp/` is gitignored (`git check-ignore .endless/tmp/x` → match) and a
  file written there does not appear in `git status`.
- No `/tmp` scratch-for-content recommendation remains in `docs/`, the guide/help
  source, or prompt templates (grep clean; intentional OS-temp uses, each
  justified, may be allow-listed).
- A fresh worktree has `.endless/tmp` present (if bootstrap-created).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1748-verify.sh
```

## Notes
- Complements E-1744 (flag gate/lint + repair) and the multiline-mirror task
  (durability). The lint that flags `/tmp` references lives in E-1744; this task
  owns the convention change + docs + gitignore so E-1744 stays focused on the
  flag-value gate.

## Goal

Make the session-status list legend **dynamic**: include only the glyphs for actions actually present in the current view, rebuilt on each frame. Today the legend is a fixed single-line `const` listing every possible glyph, and it is space-constrained — new entries (notably `⁇ other`) were left out because the full set won't fit one line. Building it from only the present actions keeps it within one line in >99% of cases and lets otherwise-omitted glyphs appear in the legend exactly when they're on screen.

## Current state (all in `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`)

- `const legend` (the fixed string) — the thing to replace.
- `action` enum + `func (action) icon()` — maps each action to its glyph; `actOther` returns `⁇` and is intentionally undocumented — today it is a catch-all for BOTH landed tasks (E-1693) and any unrecognized status. This task splits those apart (see Change).
- `classify(row)` — maps each row to its action.
- `renderTo` — prints the legend line, then the rows. Already emits the legend on every frame.
- `monitorLoop` — re-renders the whole frame each tick and repaints on change, so the legend already redraws per refresh; nothing blocks making it dynamic.

## Change

- Give each `action` a legend **label** (a table of action → {icon, label}), and derive the legend from that table instead of the hardcoded string.
- In `renderTo` (or a small helper), collect the distinct glyphs present in `rows` (reuse `classify` for actions; inspect each row for the decorations below), then build the legend from only those glyphs, in a stable order (enum order for actions, then decorations).
- **Drop the `|` group separator.** The legend is a single flat list of every glyph actually used, joined by the same two-space separator — no grouping divider.
- **Split the `⁇` catch-all into two actions** (now that the legend has room):
  - New `actLanded` — glyph **`⏚`** (electrical-ground = "landed/grounded"; decided with Mike 2026-07-09), label **`landed`**. In `classify`, change the pre-switch `if r.Landed { return actOther }` to `return actLanded`.
  - Residual `actOther` → rename to **`actUnknown`**, keep glyph `⁇`, label **`unknown`**. It now means *only* "a status the classifier doesn't recognize" — a should-never-happen safety net (every real status is already handled), so if `⁇` ever appears in the legend it flags an unhandled status slipping through. `⁇` finally matches its label.
  - Both get legend entries via the label table and appear only when a row of that kind is present.
  - Verify the `⏚` glyph is single-width with go-runewidth (as the existing `⁇` comment does) so table alignment holds.
- Include the per-row **decoration** glyphs in the same dynamic list, each shown only when a row bearing it is present:
  - `⊗ blocked` / `⏸ blocks` — the block markers (see `blockField`/the block-marker source).
  - `◆ dirty` — the `dirtyMark` glyph (worktree diverges from main / unlanded work, E-1701). **This reverses the earlier "◆ stays out of the legend" call (Mike, 2026-07-01): Mike now wants `◆` documented as `dirty`, dynamically like the rest.**
- Preserve the single-line intent. In the rare case the present set still exceeds width, prefer graceful handling (wrap or truncate) over padding with absent glyphs.

## Invariant: `session status` and `session monitor` render identically

`endless session status` (one-shot) and `endless session monitor` (redraw every 2s, `top`-style) must produce **the same output** — `monitor` is only `status` on a timer. They already share the single-frame renderer (`renderSnapshot`/`renderTo`); put the dynamic-legend logic there so both paths stay byte-identical by construction. The verify script must assert this parity (a single `status` frame equals one `monitor` frame for the same rows).

## Decisions to confirm at implementation time

- Labels resolved with Mike (2026-07-09): `⏚` = **landed**, `⁇` = **unknown**, `◆` = **dirty**.
- `internal/monitor/session_status.go` also references `⁇`. Check whether it renders its own legend needing the same treatment, or shares this path — keep scope to the `sessionstatuscmd` list view unless they share the legend.

## Out of scope

- The stale-binary symptom where `submitted` tasks render `⁇` instead of `▶` — that's fixed by rebuilding the binary (`just install` / worktree `just build`), not a code change here.

## Verify

Deliver `tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh` (model it on `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`:
pass/fail per check, `ALL PASSED` summary, exit 0 all-pass / 1 any-fail / 2 setup).
The verify-handoff to Mike must present **only**:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh

Fold every check into that script; do NOT hand Mike a manual checklist. Exercise the
renderer headlessly via the `--task` / `--from-session` / `--cols` flags (no tmux
needed) against representative row sets, asserting:

- A view with only do/plan rows → legend lists just those glyphs (no orphan/verify/
  other/blocked/blocks/dirty entries).
- A view containing a landed row → legend includes `⏚ landed` (and the row renders `⏚`).
- A view containing a row with an unrecognized status → legend includes `⁇ unknown`
  (drive this with a synthetic/unknown status value).
- A view with a blocked row → `⊗ blocked`; with a blocking row → `⏸ blocks`; with a
  dirty (worktree-diverged) row → `◆ dirty`. Each absent when no such row exists.
- The legend contains **no `|`** separator.

# Gate inline content flags against file paths + repair path-corrupted ledger fields — PLAN

## Context

Every inline multiline CLI flag (`--text`, `--description`, `--analysis`,
`--outcome`, `--justification`) stores its argument **verbatim**. Passing a file
*path* to one of these stores the path string and silently discards the intended
content. This is a footgun: the old `--text` accepted a file, but the convention
was changed so that any flag expecting a file is named `--xxxx-file` and the bare
`--xxxx` flag always means literal inline content. Agents and humans still reach
for `--text <path>`, corrupting the ledger.

Confirmed corruption at filing time (real DB):
- `tasks.text` E-1626 = `/tmp/e-1626-plan.md` — referenced file gone, no committed
  mirror `.endless/plans/E-1626.md` → likely **unrecoverable** (check git history
  `--all` before giving up). Task is `obsolete`, but repair it if a mirror turns up.
- (`tasks.outcome` E-1564 was corrupted the same way and has already been repaired
  in a resumed session — no longer in scope; the repair pass re-scans to confirm.)
- E-1202 `tasks.text` was corrupted the same way and already repaired by hand.

Guides, docs, spawn-prompt templates, and CLI help/error strings still say
`--text <path>`, actively teaching the mistake.

Two deliverables: **prevent** (a CLI gate) and **remediate** (repair data + fix
docs/guides/messages).

## Deliverable 1 — CLI gate at `_resolve_content_flag` (prevent)

Single chokepoint: `_resolve_content_flag(inline, file_path, name)` in
`src/endless/cli.py` (~line 1347). Every inline/file flag pair funnels through it
— `task add`, `task update`, `task complete`, `task assume`, `task replace`,
`decision add`, `epic add` — so one guard here covers all fields and all tables.

When `inline is not None`, apply two block rules. **Relative paths are always
allowed** — plans reference project-relative source paths (`internal/hookcmd/
claude.go`, `src/endless/cli.py`, `./tests/...`) constantly; blocking those would
make plans unwritable. Only **absolute** paths are problematic: non-portable, and
ephemeral in the `/tmp` case.

### Rule 1 — the whole value IS a path (mis-passed file)
The entire stripped value is a single whitespace-free path token — absolute OR
relative — that is path-shaped: starts with `/`, `./`, `../`, `~/`, OR contains `/`
/ ends in a file extension (`.md`/`.txt`/`.rst`/…). This is the original corruption
bug (`--text ./plan.md`, `--text /tmp/plan.md`). Block whether or not the file
exists (E-1626/E-1564 were lost precisely because a gone path was accepted). Raise
`click.ClickException` (Python f-string — this gate is Python; no Go template):
`f"--{name} received a file path ({value!r}). --{name} stores its argument "
 f"verbatim as inline content; to load a file's content use --{name}-file."`

### Rule 2 — the content CONTAINS an absolute path (anywhere)
Any token in the content that is — or after `~`-expansion / realpath becomes — an
**absolute** filesystem path (`/…`, `~/…`), appearing ANYWHERE, blocks regardless
of surrounding prose length. Relative tokens mid-content are NOT caught. (This
replaces the earlier short-wrapper / <100-char-remainder heuristic.) Existence is
not required — a gone absolute path still blocks. Message: absolute paths don't
belong in durable ledger content (non-portable; `/tmp` is lost when the worktree
drops) — put real content inline or use `--{name}-file`; for a cross-project
reference prefer a Git file URL over an absolute filesystem path.

### Escape hatch — `--allow-path=<regex>` (repeatable)
A plain, **repeatable** flag (NOT `--allow-path-file` — a path is a reference, not
file *content* like `--text-file`/`--outcome-file`). An absolute path in the
content matching ANY supplied `--allow-path` regex is exempted from both rules. For
the rare legitimate absolute path (e.g. referring to another project — though a Git
file URL is usually better).

Detection notes:
- Extract path candidates conservatively to avoid false positives on prose: treat
  `/…`-leading and `~/…`-leading tokens as candidates; expand `~`; test
  absoluteness lexically (no filesystem check — gone paths still block).
- `--allow-path` values are regexes tested against each candidate absolute path.

### Implication to weigh (flagged for Mike / implementer)
Docs and some plans reference stable absolute locations like
`~/.config/endless/endless.db` and `~/.cache/endless/...`. Under Rule 2 those are
absolute-after-`~`-expansion and will require `--allow-path` (or rephrasing). If
that friction is unwanted, a `$HOME`-relative carve-out (block `/tmp` and
other-project abs paths but permit `~/…` under `$HOME`) is the obvious tuning knob —
left as Mike's call; default is "block all absolute, escape via `--allow-path`".

Add unit tests (pytest):
- Rule 1 blocks: `/abs/x.md`, `./x.md`, `~/x.txt`, `/tmp/e-1.md` (gone or present),
  a bare `foo.md` as the whole value.
- Rule 2 blocks: `See /tmp/x.md for detail`; `the plan lives at /Users/x/plan.md`
  inside an otherwise-long paragraph; a multiline value with an absolute path on
  any line.
- Allowed: relative refs mid-content (`edit internal/hookcmd/claude.go then …`,
  `notes in ./foo.md`); multiline content whose only paths are relative; prose with
  no path.
- `--allow-path` exempts: `--text "see /opt/corp/spec.md" --allow-path '^/opt/corp/'`
  → allowed; a second, non-matching absolute path in the same content still blocks.

## Deliverable 2 — Data repair

One-shot repair (a script, not an auto-migration — this is a ledger content fix;
land per the ledger-hygiene-direct-to-main path, not a user worktree). Scan every
inline multiline column for a corrupted value — Rule 1's predicate (the whole
value is a single path token) OR Rule 2's (contains an absolute path):
- `tasks`: `text`, `description`, `analysis`, `outcome` (and `notes` if it can be
  set from an inline flag).
- `decisions`: `description` (+ any other inline multiline columns).

For each hit, recover content in priority order:
1. Committed mirror `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` — in the worktree, on `main`, or in
   git history (`git log --all -- .endless/plans/E-NNN.md`, then
   `git show <sha>:<path>`).
2. The referenced path itself, if it still exists on disk.
3. Otherwise report the row as **UNRECOVERABLE** for manual attention.

Emit a per-row report (recovered-from / unrecoverable). Do NOT silently drop
unrecoverable rows — surface them. Known unrecoverable at filing: E-1626.text
(re-verify against git `--all` first).

## Deliverable 3 — Docs / guides / error-message sweep (stop teaching it)

`grep` the repo for guidance that passes a path to an inline flag and fix each to
the `--xxxx-file` form (or clarify inline-vs-file):
- Guide markdown and the `endless guide` source, spawn-prompt templates, any
  `CLAUDE.md` snippets, and `*.py` Click help/error strings.
- Patterns: `--text <`, `--outcome <`, `--description <`, `--analysis <` followed
  by a path-looking token.
- Coordinate with the E-1202 gate message (already corrected to `--text-file`) and
  note that the E-1202 task *description* still contains the wrong `--text` form.

## Deliverable 4 — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

As part of this task, the implementing session GENERATES

  absolute path buried in a long paragraph (`… the plan is at /Users/x/plan.md …`);

- **Escape hatch**: `--text "see /opt/corp/spec.md" --allow-path '^/opt/corp/'` →
  allowed; a second non-matching absolute path in the same content still blocks;

- **Docs sweep**: no `--<inline-flag> <path>` guidance remains in `docs/` or the

- **Data repair**: the one-shot repair is a separate script that emits its own

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

## Notes

- Both rules hard-block (Mike): Rule 1 = the whole value IS a path (absolute or

# Replace /tmp with project-local .endless/tmp for scratch content — PLAN

## Context

Guides, docs, MEMORY, and spawn-prompt templates tell agents to author content at
a `/tmp/...` path, then load it (`endless task update <id> --text-file <path>`).
`/tmp` is system-global and ephemeral: if content is written there and only
*referenced* from the endless DB (the corruption class E-1744 addresses), or the
worktree is dropped before the content is loaded, it is lost to the ether — and
`/tmp` is wiped on reboot, off in a system dir no one thinks to check.

Fix: sanction a **project-local** scratch dir `.endless/tmp` and recommend it
everywhere `/tmp` is currently recommended. Co-located with the work, survives
reboot, and easy to find if content needs recovering before a worktree is dropped.

This is the **suspenders** (belt-and-suspenders with the multiline-mirror task):
mirrors preserve content that reached the DB; `.endless/tmp` keeps a
forgotten-but-not-yet-loaded scratch file recoverable instead of vaporized. Mike
wants both layers so a single forgotten step never loses important content.

## Changes

### 1. Gitignore
Add `.endless/tmp/` to the repo `.gitignore` (scratch, not tracked content — unlike
`.endless/plans/` and the new `.endless/outcomes/`). Confirm it does not shadow any
tracked `.endless/` path.

### 2. Docs / guides / MEMORY / prompt sweep
`grep` for `/tmp` recommendations and rewrite to `.endless/tmp`:
- `endless guide` source + `docs/guide*` markdown.

  path").

  temp path" — point them at `.endless/tmp`.
- User MEMORY entries that recommend `/tmp` (memory is reinforcement; the shipped
  guides/prompts are the real fix).

Be surgical: only rewrite `/tmp` uses that are **scratch-for-endless-content**
recommendations. Leave unrelated `/tmp` references (e.g. genuine OS-temp examples,
test fixtures that must use the system temp) alone — enumerate each hit and judge.

### 3. Ensure the dir exists when recommended
`.endless/tmp` must exist (or be created on demand) so the recommendation isn't a

worktree bootstrap (`post-worktree-create.sh` / `create_task_worktree`), or have
the guide instruct `mkdir -p .endless/tmp`. Prefer bootstrap creation so agents

# Version-control all multiline content as committed mirror files — PLAN

## Context

Today only a task's plan (`tasks.text`) is mirrored to a version-controlled file
`.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` (materialized + committed by `worktree_cmd.py`:
`_materialize_plan_file` / `_commit_plan_file_in_worktree`, per the E-1445/E-1525
machinery, ridden to main by worktree-land). Every OTHER multiline field —
`tasks.outcome`, `tasks.analysis`, `tasks.description`, decision bodies — lives
only in the DB. If the DB row is lost or an authoring scratch file is referenced
instead of embedded (the corruption class E-1744 addresses), that content has no
git-backed copy to recover from.

This is the **durability belt** (belt-and-suspenders with the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp`
task): even when content did make it into the DB, it should also exist as a
committed file so a human reviewing the repo on GitHub sees it and it survives a
dropped worktree / lost DB row.

## Approach

Generalize the existing plan-mirror path so it materializes+commits **every**
mirrored multiline field, not just `text`. For now, one subdir per field kind off
`.endless/` (Mike's steer — consolidate the naming convention later):
- `tasks.text`     → `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md`      (existing)
- `tasks.outcome`  → `.endless/outcomes/E-NNN.md`   (new)
- `tasks.analysis` → `.endless/analyses/E-NNN.md`   (new — analysis IS a multiline
  document field, e.g. E-1596's 9k-char analysis)
- decision bodies  → `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` (new)
- NOT `tasks.description`: a short single-line metadata field, not multiline
  document content — no file mirror. (`title` likewise excluded.)

### Mechanism (reuse, don't fork)
- Extract the plan-mirror materialize/commit into a small field-agnostic helper:
  given (task/decision id, subdir, content), write `<worktree>/.endless/<subdir>/
  <ID>.md` and stage+commit it. `_materialize_plan_file` becomes one caller.
- Call it from the same CLI write paths that already set these fields
  (`update_plan`, `add_item`, `task complete/assume/replace`, `decision add`) —
  wherever the field's content is written to the DB, also mirror it, exactly as
  `text` is mirrored now.
- Only mirrors when a worktree exists (same as today: no worktree → DB-only, the
  file is born when the worktree is created at claim/spawn). Extend
  `create_task_worktree`'s birth-time materialization to seed ALL field mirrors,
  not just the plan.
- `.gitignore`: none needed — these dirs are tracked content (like `.endless/plans`).

## Open questions (resolve in chat / at implementation)
- Confirm the multiline field set to mirror: `outcome`, `analysis`, decision
  bodies. `description`/`title` are excluded (short metadata, not documents).
- Decision ID namespace on disk (`ED-NNN.md`) — confirm the prefix matches the CLI.
- Whether to backfill existing rows' mirrors in this task or leave backfill to the
  E-1744 repair pass (recommend: birth-time + write-time here; backfill is a
  one-shot follow-up).

## Deliverable — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

The implementing session GENERATES `tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh` (self-contained,
sandbox DB, shape/output per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`) and commits it with
the implementation. It must cover:
- Set an outcome via `endless task update/complete <id> --outcome "..."` on a task
  WITH a worktree → `.endless/outcomes/E-NNN.md` is written AND committed with the
  content.
- `--outcome-file <f>` → same mirror content.
- Decision body → `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` written+committed.
- Regression: the existing `tasks.text` → `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` mirror still
  works unchanged.
- A task with no worktree → DB-only, no file written (no crash).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh
```

MANUAL (only if it can't be scripted cleanly in the sandbox): land a worktree and
confirm the outcome/decision mirrors arrive on `main` alongside the plan mirror,
and that a fresh claim/spawn seeds the mirrors at worktree birth.

## Notes
- Complements E-1744 (prevents path-corruption + repairs data) and the
  `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task (sanctioned scratch dir). Together: content is
  captured in the DB (source of truth), mirrored to git (this task), authored in a
  co-located non-ephemeral scratch dir, and protected by the flag gate.

`endless register` (`src/endless/register.py::register_project`; CLI wrapper
`cli.py::register`) is the project-init command, but today it writes only
`.endless/config.json` — it does NOT touch `.gitignore`. The existing `.endless/*`
ignore lines in this repo were added by hand, and no code writes `.gitignore`
(`purge`'s "ignore list" is endless's *discovery* ignore, i.e. `config.add_ignore`,
not git). So:
- **Add gitignore-scaffolding to `register_project`**: idempotently ensure the
  project's `.gitignore` contains the canonical endless ignore set —
  `.endless/worktrees/`, `.endless/worktree.json`, `.endless/worktree.lock`,
  `.endless/sessions/`, and the new `.endless/tmp/`. Idempotent (append only
  missing lines under a clearly-marked `# endless` block); create `.gitignore` if
  absent. This makes every newly-registered project get `.endless/tmp` (and the
  rest) automatically. Confirm the exact canonical set with Mike at implementation.
- **Backfill this repo now**: add `.endless/tmp/` to the endless project's own
  `.gitignore` by hand (register won't retroactively touch already-registered
  repos; re-running `register` on an existing project should also be safe/idempotent
  and could be the backfill path for the ~40 registered projects).

### 2. Docs / guides / MEMORY / prompt sweep

payload.title: Introduce a project command group and move project-management subcommands under it
payload.description: Endless's project commands (register, unregister, rename, set, status, list, purge, discover, scan) landed as top-level commands before the CLI adopted command groups; every later family (task, decision, epic, session, worktree, verb, tmux) is namespaced. This epic adds a 'project' group and moves the project-management commands under it for consistency. Open design question folded in: whether to add a git-init-style 'project init' and how it relates to 'register' (DB registration) vs file setup (.endless/config.json + .gitignore scaffolding).
payload.text:
# Introduce a `project` command group — EPIC

## Context

Endless's CLI grew organically. The first commands it needed were project-related
(`register`, `list`, `status`, …) and landed as TOP-LEVEL commands. As the command
count exploded, later families were namespaced under groups (`task`, `decision`,
`epic`, `channel`, `session`, `worktree`, `verb`, `tmux`, …). The original project
commands were never grouped, so they sit inconsistently at the top level. This epic
introduces a `project` group and moves the project-management commands under it, so
the CLI is consistent (`endless project register`, `endless project list`, …).

## Scope — commands to move under `project`

Currently top-level, project-scoped (confirm the exact set with Mike):
- `register`   → `project register` (or fold into `project init` — see design Q)
- `unregister` → `project unregister`
- `rename`     → `project rename`
- `set`        → `project set`
- `status`     → `project status`
- `list`       → `project list`
- `purge`      → `project purge`
- `discover`   → `project discover`
- `scan`       → `project scan`

Adjacent / decide whether they belong under `project`: `setup` (hooks/integration —
more machine than project), `docs`, `notes` (project-scoped content, but their own
families).

## Open design question — `project init` vs `register`

`init` is a familiar entry point across CLIs (`git init`, `npm init`). Two distinct
responsibilities exist today:
- **DB registration** — insert the project row (today: `register`).
- **File setup** — scaffold `.endless/config.json` and the `.gitignore` entries
  (today: partly in `register`; gitignore scaffolding is being added by the
  `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task).

Proposal (mine — open for Mike): ONE idempotent command does BOTH. A project is
unusable without both the DB row AND the on-disk files, so splitting them creates a
two-step trap ("registered but not initialized" / vice-versa). Make `project init`
the primary verb (familiar), idempotent (scaffold missing files + ensure the DB
row), with `project register` as an alias. Re-running is always safe.

If instead they stay SEPARATE (init = files, register = DB), then calling either
must detect the other's absence and either auto-run it or print the exact next
command — never leave a half-set-up project silently. But I recommend unifying.

## Back-compat

Moving top-level commands breaks muscle memory and any agent scripts calling
`endless register` / `endless list` (~40 registered projects, plus guide/prompt
text). House rule is no-legacy, but a CLI relocation is exactly where a short
transitional alias window may be warranted. Decide (Mike): hard move, or keep the
highest-traffic top-level names as thin aliases for a deprecation period.

## Relation to the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task

That task adds `.gitignore` scaffolding to `register` NOW (near-term; it unblocks
the scratch-dir durability work). That scaffolding is the "file setup" half — when
this epic reorganizes `register` → `project init`, the scaffolding moves with it.
Link: this epic relates_to that task.

## Separate investigation (do NOT bake a guess into `init`)

The canonical `.endless/` ignore set is unsettled. `.endless/worktrees/` (+ the new
`.endless/tmp/`) are definitely needed. `.endless/worktree.json`,
`.endless/worktree.lock`, `.endless/sessions/` are of UNCERTAIN currency: Mike
suspects they are obsolete, but the code still references them
(`worktree_lock.go` writes `worktree.lock`; the companion `worktree.json` is still
written/read; `session_cmd.py` reads `.endless/sessions/`, E-989) and the files
exist at the project root. Confirm-and-prune (remove the code paths AND the ignore
entries if truly dead) as its own task before `project init` freezes a canonical
ignore set. Filed/tracked separately.

## Children (file later, not now)

Break into: (a) create the `project` group + move commands (+ alias decision),
(b) `project init` unification, (c) confirm/prune the obsolete `.endless/*` files.
Do NOT create children until the alias + init/register decisions are locked.

  the lock is an `rm` that must never risk the identity; keeping them apart is
  correct, not merge-able. Both live inside worktrees (covered by
  `.endless/worktrees/`); the top-level entries are defensive for a root-level
  occurrence (a stale empty root `worktree.lock` exists today).
- **Obsolete — prune** (corroborated): `.endless/sessions/`. Nothing WRITES it
  (the only writer in code is `worktree.json`); its 7 files are all 2+ months
  stale; the lone reference is a stale docstring at
  `session_cmd.py::session_show_resolve` (data actually comes from the DB
  `sessions` table + tmux, not the files dir). Child (c): remove the dead read/
  docstring path, delete the dir, and DROP the `.endless/sessions/` ignore entry —
  do this before `project init` freezes the canonical set.

## Children (file later, not now)

Break into: (a) create the `project` group + move commands (+ alias decision),
(b) `project init` unification, (c) confirm/prune the obsolete `.endless/*` files.
Do NOT create children until the alias + init/register decisions are locked.

payload.title: Backfill mirror files for pre-existing outcome/analysis/decision content

fields.description: E-1747 added write-time and worktree-birth mirroring of tasks.outcome, tasks.analysis, and decision bodies to committed .endless/{outcomes,analyses,decisions}/ files, but only for content written from now on. Rows that already carry outcome/analysis in the DB (and existing decisions) have no mirror file yet. This is a one-shot pass to generate and commit mirrors for that pre-existing content: for each task with a live worktree, materialize its outcome/analysis mirrors; for decisions, write ED-NNN.md to the appropriate location. Deferred out of E-1747 by Mike's steer (write-time + birth-time only there).

payload.title: Split worktree identity (worktree.json) from ownership lock (worktree.lock)
payload.description: Each endless-managed worktree keeps two separate files under its .endless/: worktree.json holds write-once IDENTITY (kind, base_branch, branch, created_at) — set at creation, never changed for the worktree's life; worktree.lock holds write-often OWNERSHIP (session_id, pid, tmux_pane, claimed_at) — written on claim, deleted on release, rewritten by the next session. They are kept separate BECAUSE their lifecycles differ: releasing a worktree removes the lock (an rm), which must never touch or risk corrupting the durable identity, and a crash mid-lock-write cannot damage identity; the identity persists across sessions while the lock churns per session. Merging them would couple ephemeral ownership churn to write-once identity — an anti-goal. This ADR documents existing shipped design (the E-971 worktree foundation); no code change. Written after a session mistook the two files for a mergeable redundancy.

# Introduce a `project` command group — EPIC

## Context

Endless's CLI grew organically. The first commands it needed were project-related
(`register`, `list`, `status`, …) and landed as TOP-LEVEL commands. As the command
count exploded, later families were namespaced under groups (`task`, `decision`,
`epic`, `channel`, `session`, `worktree`, `verb`, `tmux`, …). The original project
commands were never grouped, so they sit inconsistently at the top level. This epic
introduces a `project` group and moves the project-management commands under it, so
the CLI is consistent (`endless project register`, `endless project list`, …).

## Scope — commands to move under `project`

Currently top-level, project-scoped (confirm the exact set with Mike):
- `register`   → `project register` (or fold into `project init` — see design Q)
- `unregister` → `project unregister`
- `rename`     → `project rename`
- `set`        → `project set`
- `status`     → `project status`
- `list`       → `project list`
- `purge`      → `project purge`
- `discover`   → `project discover`
- `scan`       → `project scan`

Adjacent / decide whether they belong under `project`: `setup` (hooks/integration —
more machine than project), `docs`, `notes` (project-scoped content, but their own
families).

## Decision (Mike) — `project init`, unified, `register` as alias

`init` is a familiar entry point across CLIs (`git init`, `npm init`). Two
responsibilities exist today: **DB registration** (insert the project row — today
`register`) and **file setup** (scaffold `.endless/config.json` + `.gitignore`
entries — today partly in `register`; gitignore scaffolding added by the
`/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task).

DECIDED: unify. ONE idempotent `project init` does BOTH — scaffolds missing files
AND ensures the DB row — because a project is unusable without both, and splitting
them creates a half-set-up trap. `project init` is the primary verb; `project
register` is an alias for the same command. Re-running is always safe (idempotent).

## Back-compat — decided (Mike): hidden hard-error stubs

The old top-level names (`endless register`, `endless list`, …) become **hidden
hard-error stubs**: invoking one exits non-zero with a message naming the new
command (`use 'endless project register'`). They do NOT work as aliases, and they
do NOT appear in `--help` (hidden). This surfaces the move loudly to anyone (agent
or human) still calling the old name, without silently papering over it. The stubs
are a temporary migration aid — a later task removes them entirely.

## Relation to the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task

That task adds `.gitignore` scaffolding to `register` NOW (near-term; it unblocks
the scratch-dir durability work). That scaffolding is the "file setup" half — when
this epic reorganizes `register` → `project init`, the scaffolding moves with it.
Link: this epic relates_to that task.

## Separate investigation (do NOT bake a guess into `init`)

The canonical `.endless/` ignore set (which `project init` will scaffold):
- **Live, keep**: `.endless/worktrees/` and the new `.endless/tmp/`.
- **Live, keep, but distinct by design** — `.endless/worktree.json` (write-once
  worktree IDENTITY: kind/base_branch/branch/created_at) and
  `.endless/worktree.lock` (write-often OWNERSHIP: session_id/pid/pane/claimed_at,
  deleted on release). Separate files because their lifecycles differ — releasing
  the lock is an `rm` that must never risk the identity; keeping them apart is
  correct, not merge-able. Both live inside worktrees (covered by
  `.endless/worktrees/`); the top-level entries are defensive for a root-level
  occurrence (a stale empty root `worktree.lock` exists today).
- **Obsolete — prune** (corroborated): `.endless/sessions/`. Nothing WRITES it
  (the only writer in code is `worktree.json`); its 7 files are all 2+ months
  stale; the lone reference is a stale docstring at
  `session_cmd.py::session_show_resolve` (data actually comes from the DB
  `sessions` table + tmux, not the files dir). Child (c): remove the dead read/
  docstring path, delete the dir, and DROP the `.endless/sessions/` ignore entry —
  do this before `project init` freezes the canonical set.

## Children (filed — decisions locked)

- (a) Create the `project` group + move the 9 commands under it; leave hidden
  hard-error top-level stubs.
- (b) Build the unified `project init` (idempotent files + DB); `register` alias.
  Blocked by (a).
- (c) Confirm-and-prune the obsolete `.endless/sessions/` files. Should land before
  (b) freezes the canonical `.gitignore` set.

Related ADR: ED-1530 (why worktree.json and worktree.lock stay separate).

Confirm no live reader/writer remains, remove the dead path + stale docstring, delete the dir, and drop the .endless/sessions/ gitignore entry.

Parent epic: the `project` command group. Independent of (a)/(b), but should land
BEFORE (b) freezes the canonical `.gitignore` set (so the obsolete entry is never
scaffolded into new projects).

## Finding (this session)
`.endless/sessions/` is obsolete: nothing WRITES it (the only remaining
companion-file writer is `worktree.json`); the files are 2+ months stale; the sole
code reference is a STALE docstring on `session_show_resolve` in

## Scope
1. Confirm no live writer/reader remains (re-grep for `.endless/sessions`,

4. Drop the `.endless/sessions/` entry from this repo's `.gitignore`, and ensure the

## Deliverable — verify script
Generate `tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh` (shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`):
`grep` shows no live `.endless/sessions` read/write path in `src/endless/`; `endless
session show`/`list` still work (data from DB + tmux); `.endless/sessions/` is not

# (b) Build the unified `project init` command — PLAN

Parent epic: the `project` command group. Blocked by child (a) (the `project` group
must exist first).

## Decision (from the epic)
Unify DB registration and file setup into ONE idempotent `project init`:
- Ensures the project's DB row (today `register_project` in `src/endless/register.py`).
- Scaffolds on-disk files: `.endless/config.json` (existing) + the `.gitignore`
  entries (see the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task, which adds gitignore-scaffolding).
- `project register` becomes an alias for `project init` (same behavior).
- Re-running is always safe (scaffold only what is missing; don't clobber).

## Canonical `.gitignore` set to scaffold
- `.endless/worktrees/` and `.endless/tmp/` (definite).
- `.endless/worktree.json`, `.endless/worktree.lock` (kept — see ADR ED-1530).
- NOT `.endless/sessions/` — child (c) prunes it; land (c) before this freezes the
  set so the obsolete entry is never scaffolded into new projects.

## Deliverable — verify script
Generate `tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh` (shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`):
`project init` on a throwaway git repo creates the DB row AND scaffolds
`.endless/config.json` + the canonical `.gitignore` set; re-running is idempotent
(no dup rows, no dup gitignore lines); `project register` behaves identically. On
completion, set `unverified` and hand off exactly:
`esu && ./tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh`.

payload.title: Add a handoff-status command that reports only out-of-band git anomalies
payload.description: On session handoff the agent narrates git side-effects (uncommitted files, stray tags, unlanded commits, leaked worktrees, working-tree cleanliness). Because the spawn prompt enumerates these as categories to report, a clean repo yields 'nothing to report' dressed as reporting — pure noise. Provide a command that inspects the repo itself and prints ONLY non-empty findings; a clean state prints nothing. The agent's final message then reduces to what it genuinely can't compute: how-to-verify and the return line. This moves the 'is clean worth saying?' judgment out of the agent (which errs toward self-covering) into a tool where empty output IS the representation of clean — the durable fix for this class of noise.

payload.title: Rewrite spawn-prompt final-message template from enumerated categories to a single exception rule
payload.description: The spawn-prompt template's closing instructions enumerate report categories (git side-effects, landed-vs-worktree delta, external state). Naming an empty category invites the agent to fill it with 'none'. Replace the enumeration with one rule: state a delta only if it is anomalous; otherwise emit nothing but the verification steps and the return line. Removing the buckets removes the prompt to confirm-the-negative. Cheap, immediate mitigation while the handoff-status command (the durable fix) is built.

payload.title: Lint gate that bounces negative-confirmation ceremony in agent handoffs
payload.description: A gate — same spirit as the Haiku verb-check — that flags negative-confirmation patterns in an agent's final handoff/report ('no stray X', 'nothing to report', 'confirmed clean', 'as expected', '(should be empty)') and asks the agent to drop them, catching the noise regardless of how the template is worded. Filed as brainstorm because the mechanism needs discussion before it is actionable: where/how a 'final handoff' is intercepted (unlike a git commit it is not a discrete artifact), whether pattern-matching is viable without excessive false positives, and whether this belongs as a hook, a verb-check-style check, or plain guidance.

# E-1750 — Make the session-status legend dynamic

## Context

The session-status list legend is a fixed one-line `const` that hardcodes every
possible glyph. Because it must fit one line, otherwise-useful glyphs were left
out (notably `⁇`, and the `◆ dirty` marker) — the line has no room. Building the
legend from only the actions/decorations actually present in the current frame
keeps it within one line in >99% of cases and lets an omitted glyph appear
exactly when it's on screen. This also lets us split today's `⁇` catch-all (which
conflates *landed* and *unrecognized-status*) into two documented glyphs.

All work is in one Go file plus its test and a new verify script. No product
behavior outside the legend/classification changes.

## Changes — `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`

1. **Action metadata table.** Replace the standalone `func (a action) icon()`
   with a table carrying both glyph and legend label, indexed by the `action`
   enum so enum order == legend order for free:

   ```go
   var actionMeta = [...]struct{ icon, label string }{
       actThis:    {"●", "this"},
       actParent:  {"↑", "parent"},
       actFrom:    {"↩", "from"},
       actDoing:   {"⟳", "doing"},
       actDo:      {"▶", "do"},
       actPlan:    {"✎", "plan"},
       actVerify:  {"☑", "verify"},
       actOrphan:  {"◷", "orphan"},
       actLanded:  {"⏚", "landed"},
       actUnknown: {"⁇", "unknown"},
   }
   func (a action) icon() string  { return actionMeta[a].icon }
   func (a action) label() string { return actionMeta[a].label }
   ```

2. **Split the `⁇` catch-all.** Extend the enum from `…, actOrphan, actOther`
   to `…, actOrphan, actLanded, actUnknown` (append only — do not reorder the
   existing members, since `sortRows` ranks on the enum). In `classify`:
   - `if r.Landed { return actLanded }` (was `actOther`).
   - `default: return actUnknown` (was `actOther`).
   `actUnknown` now means *only* "a status the classifier doesn't recognize" — a
   should-never-happen safety net; `⁇` finally matches its `unknown` label.
   Update the `actLanded`/`actUnknown` doc comments accordingly (drop the
   "intentionally undocumented" note — both are now in the label table).

3. **Delete `const legend`.** Add `buildLegend`:

   ```go
   // buildLegend returns the dynamic header: only the glyphs actually present in
   // rows, in enum order (actions) then fixed order (decorations), two-space-
   // joined, no group separator. Rebuilt each frame by renderTo, so `session
   // status` and `session monitor` stay byte-identical by construction.
   func buildLegend(rows []monitor.SessionStatusRow) string {
       var present [len(actionMeta)]bool
       var blocked, blocks, dirty bool
       for _, r := range rows {
           present[classify(r)] = true
           if r.BlockedByN > 0 { blocked = true }
           if r.BlocksN > 0    { blocks = true }
           if r.Dirty          { dirty = true }
       }
       var parts []string
       for a := action(0); int(a) < len(actionMeta); a++ {
           if present[a] { parts = append(parts, a.icon()+" "+a.label()) }
       }
       if blocked { parts = append(parts, "⊗ blocked") }
       if blocks  { parts = append(parts, "⏸ blocks") }
       if dirty   { parts = append(parts, "◆ dirty") }
       return strings.Join(parts, "  ")
   }
   ```

   Decoration glyphs/labels are inline string literals (the `⊗`/`⏸` match
   `blockField`, `◆` matches `dirtyMark`); a tiny local table is an acceptable
   alternative if it reads cleaner at implementation time.

4. **`renderTo`** — emit the dynamic legend, and only when there are rows to
   document. Move the legend print *below* the empty/no-task guard so the no-task
   view shows just the hint (no blank/empty legend line):

   ```go
   func renderTo(...) {
       if focal == 0 || len(rows) == 0 {
           fmt.Fprintln(w, dim(noTaskHint, color))
           return
       }
       sortRows(rows)
       fmt.Fprintln(w, dim(buildLegend(rows), color))
       // …existing block-width + per-row rendering unchanged…
   }
   ```

   Single-line intent: since only present glyphs are included there is never any
   absent-glyph padding; in the rare case the present set still exceeds width the
   terminal soft-wraps (acceptable — no truncation, which would hide a real
   glyph). No `cols` argument needed by `buildLegend`.

5. **`⏚` width guard.** Confirm `runewidth.StringWidth("⏚") == 1` (as the `⁇`
   comment already asserts) so the fixed 13-col prefix alignment holds; document
   it in the `actLanded` comment. If it measures wide, stop and reconsider the
   glyph before proceeding.

## Tests — `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status_test.go`

- **`TestClassify`**: retarget the existing cases — `Status:"blocked"` and the
  three `landed …` cases now expect `actUnknown` / `actLanded` respectively
  (currently `actOther`).
- **`TestActionIcons`**: add `actLanded`→`⏚`, `actUnknown`→`⁇`.
- **New `TestBuildLegend`** (table-driven, constructs rows directly): asserts, at
  minimum —
  - do+plan rows only → `"▶ do  ✎ plan"` (no orphan/verify/landed/unknown/
    blocked/blocks/dirty).
  - a `Landed` row → contains `"⏚ landed"`.
  - an unrecognized `Status` (e.g. `"blocked"`) → contains `"⁇ unknown"`.
  - `BlockedByN>0` → `"⊗ blocked"`; `BlocksN>0` → `"⏸ blocks"`; `Dirty:true` →
    `"◆ dirty"`; each absent when no such row. **This is the sole coverage of
    `◆ dirty`** (a real divergent worktree can't be seeded hermetically in bash —
    decided with Mike).
  - output contains no `"|"`.
  - a full/mixed row set orders actions in enum order then decorations.

## Verify — `tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh`

Model on `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh` (per-check pass/fail, `ALL PASSED`
summary, exit 0 all-pass / 1 any-fail / 2 setup). Handoff to Mike is exactly:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh

Check groups, all folded into the one script:

1. **Legend logic (hermetic).** Run `go test ./internal/sessionstatuscmd/...` —
   green covers `TestBuildLegend` (incl. `◆ dirty`), `TestClassify`,
   `TestActionIcons`.
2. **End-to-end binary path**, seeding the sandbox DB and driving
   `./bin/endless-go session-status --task <id> [--from-session <id>] --cols <n>`
   (headless; no tmux). Build rows as children/dependents of a focal task:
   - do+plan-only focal tree → legend lists just `▶ do` / `✎ plan`, and asserts
     **absence** of orphan/verify/landed/unknown/blocked/blocks/dirty entries.
   - a landed child (`endless worktree land <id> --record-only --sha <dummy>`) →
     legend contains `⏚ landed` and the row renders `⏚`.
   - a blocked child (`task add --blocked-by <open id>`) → `⊗ blocked`; a
     blocking child (`task add --blocks <id>`) → `⏸ blocks`; each absent
     otherwise.
   - an unknown-status child (`task update --status blocked`, falling back to the
     Go test if the CLI's status guard refuses it) → `⁇ unknown`.
   - the legend contains no `|`.
   - **parity:** one `session status` frame is byte-identical to one
     `session monitor` frame for the same rows — `diff <(… --task N --cols C)
     <(… --task N --monitor --cols C)` (piped `--monitor` degrades to a single
     snapshot, so this proves the shared renderer).

Use the worktree-built binary directly (`./bin/endless-go …`, self-detects the
sandbox from cwd) and route CLI seeding through `--db sandbox` like the e-1577
model.

## Out of scope

- `internal/monitor/session_status.go`'s `⁇` mentions (SQL comments only — no
  second legend).
- The stale-binary symptom where `submitted` renders `⁇` instead of `▶` (fixed by
  rebuilding, not code here).

## Steps

1. Edit `session_status.go` (enum, `actionMeta`, `buildLegend`, `classify`,
   `renderTo`, comments).
2. Update/extend `session_status_test.go`; `just build` then
   `go test ./internal/sessionstatuscmd/...` until green.
3. Write `tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh`; run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1750-verify.sh`.
4. `endless task update E-1750 --status unverified --db main`; hand Mike the
   one-line test command + return line.

# E-1754 — Backfill mirror files for pre-existing doc content — PLAN

## Context

E-1747 mirrors `tasks.{text,outcome,analysis}` and decision bodies to committed
`.endless/{plans,outcomes,analyses,decisions}/…md` files, but only for content
written from now on. Rows that already hold outcome/analysis (and existing
decisions, and any task whose text never got a plan file) have no mirror yet.
This is the one-shot pass that fills those gaps so the durability belt covers
history.

## Approach

A one-shot command, run FROM the E-1754 worktree, reconciles every document
field for the worktree's project into committed mirror files **on the E-1754
worktree branch** — the files then ride the normal `worktree land` to main. No
direct-to-main commits; no per-file commit storm.

Fill gaps only: write a mirror **only when the target file is absent**. It never
overwrites an existing file, so it can't reconcile drift or rewrite the hundreds
of plan files already on main — and re-running is trivially a no-op.

## Mechanism

New Go one-shot (DB reads are Go-only, E-894), e.g.
`endless-go event backfill-doc-mirrors` — resolves the worktree root + project
from cwd, then:

1. Reads, for the worktree's project: tasks with non-empty `text` / `outcome` /
   `analysis`, and decisions with a non-empty body. One bulk query each (reuse
   `monitor` DB access; the column whitelist / subdir map mirrors E-1747's
   `_TASK_DOC_FIELDS`: text→plans, outcome→outcomes, analysis→analyses; decision
   body→decisions with the `ED-` prefix).
2. For each, if `<wt>/.endless/<subdir>/E-NNN.md` (or `ED-NNN.md`) is **absent**,
   writes it (creating the subdir). Present → skip.
3. Stages all newly-written paths and makes ONE commit on the worktree branch:
   `Endless: backfill doc mirrors (N files)`. Plain `git -C <wt> add/commit` —
   NOT `events.commitPaths`, which refuses linked worktrees (`ensureMainCheckout`).
   Zero new files → no commit.

Python CLI: a thin admin wrapper to invoke it (surfaced verb TBD at
implementation, e.g. `endless task backfill-mirrors`), or run the endless-go
command directly.

## Scope

- Fields: all four — text, outcome, analysis, decision bodies.
- Project: the worktree's project only (endless). Other projects, if they adopt
  the committed-mirror convention, run their own backfill later — out of scope.

## Deliverable — verify script

Generate `tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh` (isolated env, shape per
`tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh`). Seed a project + a git worktree; create tasks
carrying outcome/analysis (and text) with NO per-task worktree, plus a decision;
run the backfill from the worktree. Assert:
- the expected `.endless/{plans,outcomes,analyses}/E-NNN.md` and
  `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` appear in the worktree AND are in one commit.
- a task/decision with empty fields produces no file.
- an already-present mirror is left untouched (gap-fill, not overwrite).
- re-running the backfill makes no second commit (idempotent).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

Set `unverified`; tell Mike to run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh`.

# Let projects configure their own allowed paths for the path gate — PLAN

Phase: later. Relates to the inline-content path gate (E-1744).

## Context
The path gate (E-1744) blocks absolute paths in inline flag content. Its built-in
**allowed paths** — a data-driven *table* of endless's own resolved dirs
(`<config_dir>/endless/`, `<cache_dir>/endless/`, XDG-resolved, NOT hardcoded) —
exempt the well-known endless locations that legitimately appear in plans from
outside the project root, so a user need not pass `--allow-path` for them.

But endless is used as a PRODUCT by ~40 other projects, each with its OWN
well-known outside-root paths that legitimately appear in that project's plans
(build dirs, shared toolchains, sibling repos, etc.). Those projects need a way to
declare their allowed paths once, rather than passing `--allow-path` on every
command.

## Approach
- Add an `allowed_paths` array (list of absolute-path regexes) to project config
  `.endless/config.json`.
- The gate composes its effective allowed set from ONE table/merge point:
  built-in endless dirs (E-1744's table) + project-config `allowed_paths` +
  per-invocation `--allow-path` flags. Reuse the exact table mechanism E-1744
  establishes — extend the table from config, don't fork the logic.
- Terminology: **"allowed paths"** everywhere (config key, docs, help) — NOT
  "whitelist".

## Pull-forward note
If E-1744's built-in table is structured so that merging a config-provided
`allowed_paths` array is trivial, this can be folded into E-1744 now rather than
waiting. Filed `later` because it's the downstream-product surface, not needed for
endless's own self-dev use; promote if the config merge turns out to be a few lines.

## Deliverable — verify script
Generate `tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh` (shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`):
an absolute path matching a project-config `allowed_paths` entry is accepted; a
non-matching absolute path still blocks; built-in endless dirs and `--allow-path`
still work. On completion set `unverified` and hand off exactly:
`esu && ./tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh`.
