# Worked example — negative-confirmation ceremony in a real agent handoff

This is a verbatim transcript of a live E-1748 session handoff and the correction
that followed. It is a concrete specimen for the lint gate this task proposes:
the spans a gate would need to catch, and — importantly — a second-order failure
mode (meta-ceremony) that a naive phrase-matcher would miss. Annotations mark
what the gate should flag and why.

---

## Turn 1 — the agent's handoff (the offending output)

> Everything is complete and the working tree is clean. Here's my handoff.
>
> **What `session status` can't show**
>
> **Git / worktree side-effects**
> - One commit on `task/1748-…` (`4e5c6108`), working tree **clean**. 6 files … ready for you to land.
> - **Two MEMORY files edited outside the repo** (`~/.claude/…/memory/`) … they live outside the branch, so they persist regardless of land/drop and won't travel with the merge.
> - `.endless/tmp/` empty dir now exists in this worktree (gitignored, harmless). `bin/endless-go` was rebuilt by `just build` (gitignored).
> - The verify script registers then unregisters a throwaway project in the **sandbox** DB each run — net-clean, never touches the real ledger.
>
> **State outside endless**: none — no CI, no external services involved.
>
> **How to test**
> ```
> esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1748-verify.sh
> ```
> … [how-to-test + return line] …

**Annotation.** Of everything above, exactly one line is signal the reviewer
could not compute: *the two MEMORY files edited outside the branch*. Plus the
how-to-test and the return line. Everything else is negative-confirmation
ceremony, and it appeared because the spawn prompt enumerates report *categories*
— "git side-effects", "state outside endless" — and an empty named bucket invites
the agent to write "none" into it. Phrases a gate should catch here:

- "the working tree is clean" / "working tree **clean**"
- "gitignored, harmless"
- "net-clean, never touches the real ledger"
- "**State outside endless**: none — no CI, no external services involved"

## Turn 2 — the user's pushback

> Regarding that "report" see E-1758, E-1759, E-1760 and then let me know what I
> ACTUALLY needed to know?

## Turn 3 — the agent concedes and strips it down

> You're right — most of that "report" was confirm-the-negative ceremony. …
> What you **actually** needed was three things: (1) the two MEMORY files I
> edited live outside the branch; (2) how to verify; (3) the return line.
> **Everything else — the clean working tree, the committed 6-file delta,
> "nothing on main yet", the sandbox being net-clean, the gitignored
> `.endless/tmp/` and rebuilt binary — is either already visible to you or is the
> absence of a problem, which needs no words. Empty output is the correct
> representation of clean.**

**Annotation — the second-order failure.** The bolded closing paragraph is the
subtle one. It contains no "no stray X" / "confirmed clean" tokens, yet it is
*still* ceremony: it inventories the silence — it re-lists every clean thing in
order to announce that clean things need no words. A phrase-based gate keyed on a
fixed deny-list ("nothing to report", "as expected") would pass this paragraph.
This is the hard case the task must reckon with.

## Turn 4 — the user names the second-order failure

> Wouldn't it also be fair to say that the last paragraph was also "negative
> ceremony?"

## Turn 5 — the agent agrees

> Yes — and worse than the first pass: it was *meta*-ceremony. I listed
> everything I was omitting and explained why it was noise, which is more words
> than just omitting it would have been. The right version stops after the three
> items. No inventory of the silence.

---

## What the gate has to detect (design implications)

1. **Surface deny-list is necessary but not sufficient.** Tokens like "no stray",
   "nothing to report", "confirmed clean", "(should be empty)", "as expected"
   catch Turn 1 but miss Turn 3's inventory-of-the-silence paragraph.
2. **The deeper signal is structural, not lexical:** a handoff that enumerates
   items only to assert they carry no consequence. "Everything else … needs no
   words" is itself the tell — an agent explaining what it chose not to say.
3. **The correct handoff shape** (target state the gate rewards): genuine
   out-of-band anomalies only + how-to-verify + return line. An empty category
   yields zero characters, never "none". No trailing paragraph accounting for the
   omissions.
4. **Open question this example sharpens:** can pattern-matching alone
   distinguish "the two MEMORY files won't land with the branch" (keep — a real
   anomaly) from "the working tree is clean" (drop — a non-event) without an
   LLM-judge pass? Turn 3 shows even a careful agent, asked to self-correct,
   produced fresh ceremony — which argues the check cannot be purely the agent's
   own judgment (it "errs toward self-covering", per E-1758's framing).

fields.text: See the analysis field for a verbatim worked example: a real E-1748 session handoff whose report was almost entirely negative-confirmation ceremony, the user's two rounds of pushback, and — critically — a second-order 'meta-ceremony' failure (an inventory-of-the-silence paragraph) that a fixed phrase deny-list would NOT catch. Use it as the reference specimen when designing the gate: it grounds the false-positive/false-negative boundary and shows even a self-correcting agent re-introduced ceremony, which bears on whether the check can rely on the agent's own judgment.

# E-1754 — Backfill mirror files for pre-existing doc content — PLAN

## Context

E-1747 mirrors `tasks.{text,outcome,analysis}` and decision bodies to committed
`.endless/{plans,outcomes,analyses,decisions}/…md` files, but only for content
written from now on. Rows that already hold outcome/analysis (and existing
decisions, and any task whose text never got a plan file) have no mirror yet.
This is the one-shot pass that fills those gaps so the durability belt covers
history.

## Approach

A one-shot command, run FROM the E-1754 worktree, reconciles every document
field for the worktree's project into committed mirror files **on the E-1754
worktree branch** — the files then ride the normal `worktree land` to main. No
direct-to-main commits; no per-file commit storm.

Fill gaps only: write a mirror **only when the target file is absent**. It never
overwrites an existing file, so it can't reconcile drift or rewrite the hundreds
of plan files already on main — and re-running is trivially a no-op.

## Mechanism — a persisted one-off migration artifact, NOT a CLI command

Mike's steer: no user-facing verb (dead surface after its one run). DB reads are
Go-only (E-894), so the write logic is Go — but shaped as a persisted one-off
that never enters either binary's command surface:

- A `//go:build ignore` `package main` program (same build-excluded form as the
  `internal/schema/changes/e-NNN-*.go` migrations), run explicitly via
  `go run <file>`. `go build ./...` skips it; `endless`/`endless-go` never grow a
  subcommand. It does NOT use the schema-changes runner — that runner is
  DDL-specific (wraps each change in a DB transaction, records `_schema_version`);
  this one reads the DB read-only and mutates files + git.
- Recommended home: a dedicated `migrations/e-1754-backfill-doc-mirrors.go` (I'm
  proposing a top-level `migrations/` since `internal/schema/changes/` is the
  DDL-via-runner home and would mislead the land dispatcher into auto-applying
  it). Open to Mike moving it at approval.

What it does, run from the E-1754 worktree:

1. Reads, for the worktree's project: tasks with non-empty `text` / `outcome` /
   `analysis`, and decisions with a non-empty body. One bulk query each (reuse
   `internal/monitor` DB access; the column→subdir map mirrors E-1747's
   `_TASK_DOC_FIELDS`: text→plans, outcome→outcomes, analysis→analyses; decision
   body→decisions with the `ED-` prefix).
2. For each, if `<wt>/.endless/<subdir>/E-NNN.md` (or `ED-NNN.md`) is **absent**,
   writes it (creating the subdir). Present → skip (gap-fill, never overwrites).
3. Stages all newly-written paths and makes ONE commit on the worktree branch:
   `Endless: backfill doc mirrors (N files)`. Plain `git -C <wt> add/commit` —
   NOT `events.commitPaths`, which refuses linked worktrees (`ensureMainCheckout`).
   Zero new files → no commit.

Re-runnable and idempotent (gap-fill means a second run finds every file present
and writes nothing). Precedent for a persisted, re-runnable backfill driver:
`tests/tasks/e-1719-backfill.sh`.

## Scope

- Fields: all four — text, outcome, analysis, decision bodies.
- Project: the worktree's project only (endless). Other projects, if they adopt
  the committed-mirror convention, run their own backfill later — out of scope.

## Deliverable — verify script

Generate `tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh` (isolated env, shape per
`tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh`). Seed a project + a git worktree; create tasks
carrying outcome/analysis (and text) with NO per-task worktree, plus a decision;
run the backfill from the worktree via `go run migrations/e-1754-backfill-doc-mirrors.go`.
Assert:
- the expected `.endless/{plans,outcomes,analyses}/E-NNN.md` and
  `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` appear in the worktree AND are in one commit.
- a task/decision with empty fields produces no file.
- an already-present mirror is left untouched (gap-fill, not overwrite).
- re-running the backfill makes no second commit (idempotent).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

Set `unverified`; tell Mike to run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh`.
MANUAL: in the real E-1754 worktree, run the backfill; `git log`/`git status`
show one `backfill doc mirrors` commit with the expected new files; then land
E-1754 normally and confirm the mirrors arrive on main.

## Notes

- Reuses E-1747: the field→subdir convention and file layout; `internal/monitor`
  for reads. The genuinely new piece is the bulk read + single worktree-branch
  commit, packaged as a build-excluded one-off (no command surface).
- Not a legacy command: nothing is added to `endless` / `endless-go`. The
  artifact persists like a dated migration and is re-runnable via `go run`.

# Gate inline content flags against file paths + repair path-corrupted ledger fields — PLAN

## Context

Every inline multiline CLI flag (`--text`, `--description`, `--analysis`,
`--outcome`, `--justification`) stores its argument **verbatim**. Passing a file
*path* to one of these stores the path string and silently discards the intended
content. This is a footgun: the old `--text` accepted a file, but the convention
was changed so that any flag expecting a file is named `--xxxx-file` and the bare
`--xxxx` flag always means literal inline content. Agents and humans still reach
for `--text <path>`, corrupting the ledger.

Confirmed corruption at filing time (real DB):
- `tasks.text` E-1626 = `/tmp/e-1626-plan.md` — referenced file gone, no committed
  mirror `.endless/plans/E-1626.md` → likely **unrecoverable** (check git history
  `--all` before giving up). Task is `obsolete`, but repair it if a mirror turns up.
- (`tasks.outcome` E-1564 was corrupted the same way and has already been repaired
  in a resumed session — no longer in scope; the repair pass re-scans to confirm.)
- E-1202 `tasks.text` was corrupted the same way and already repaired by hand.

Guides, docs, spawn-prompt templates, and CLI help/error strings still say
`--text <path>`, actively teaching the mistake.

Two deliverables: **prevent** (a CLI gate) and **remediate** (repair data + fix
docs/guides/messages).

## Deliverable 1 — CLI gate at `_resolve_content_flag` (prevent)

Single chokepoint: `_resolve_content_flag(inline, file_path, name)` in
`src/endless/cli.py` (~line 1347). Every inline/file flag pair funnels through it
— `task add`, `task update`, `task complete`, `task assume`, `task replace`,
`decision add`, `epic add` — so one guard here covers all fields and all tables.

When `inline is not None`, apply two block rules. **Relative paths are always
allowed** — plans reference project-relative source paths (`internal/hookcmd/
claude.go`, `src/endless/cli.py`, `./tests/...`) constantly; blocking those would
make plans unwritable. Only **absolute** paths are problematic: non-portable, and
ephemeral in the `/tmp` case.

### Rule 1 — the whole value IS a path (mis-passed file)
The entire stripped value is a single whitespace-free path token — absolute OR
relative — that is path-shaped: starts with `/`, `./`, `../`, `~/`, OR contains `/`
/ ends in a file extension (`.md`/`.txt`/`.rst`/…). This is the original corruption
bug (`--text ./plan.md`, `--text /tmp/plan.md`). Block whether or not the file
exists (E-1626/E-1564 were lost precisely because a gone path was accepted). Raise
`click.ClickException` (Python f-string — this gate is Python; no Go template):
`f"--{name} received a file path ({value!r}). --{name} stores its argument "
 f"verbatim as inline content; to load a file's content use --{name}-file."`

### Rule 2 — the content CONTAINS an absolute path (anywhere)
Any token in the content that is — or after `~`-expansion / realpath becomes — an
**absolute** filesystem path (`/…`, `~/…`), appearing ANYWHERE, blocks regardless
of surrounding prose length. Relative tokens mid-content are NOT caught. (This
replaces the earlier short-wrapper / <100-char-remainder heuristic.) Existence is
not required — a gone absolute path still blocks. Message: absolute paths don't
belong in durable ledger content (non-portable; `/tmp` is lost when the worktree
drops) — put real content inline or use `--{name}-file`; for a cross-project
reference prefer a Git file URL over an absolute filesystem path.

### Escape hatch — `--allow-path=<regex>` (repeatable)
A plain, **repeatable** flag (NOT `--allow-path-file` — a path is a reference, not
file *content* like `--text-file`/`--outcome-file`). An absolute path in the
content matching ANY supplied `--allow-path` regex is exempted from both rules. For
the rare legitimate absolute path (e.g. referring to another project — though a Git
file URL is usually better).

Detection notes:
- Extract path candidates conservatively to avoid false positives on prose: treat
  `/…`-leading and `~/…`-leading tokens as candidates; expand `~`; test
  absoluteness lexically (no filesystem check — gone paths still block).
- `--allow-path` values are regexes tested against each candidate absolute path.

### Built-in allowed paths (decided) — endless's own config + cache dirs
Docs and plans legitimately reference stable endless-owned locations outside the
project root (`<config_dir>/endless/…` and `<cache_dir>/endless/…` — e.g.
`~/.config/endless/endless.db`, `~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/…`). These are ALWAYS
exempt from both rules, with NO `--allow-path` needed:
- Build the exempt set as a data-driven **table** of resolved endless dirs — NOT an
  `if`/`switch`. Resolve via endless's own config/cache-dir resolution (honors
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME`); do NOT hardcode `~/.config/endless`.
- One composition point: effective allowed set = built-in table + per-invocation
  `--allow-path` regexes (+ later, project-config `allowed_paths` — see follow-up
  task). Apply to Rule 1 and Rule 2 alike.
- Terminology: **"allowed paths"**, never "whitelist".

Add unit tests (pytest):
- Rule 1 blocks: `/abs/x.md`, `./x.md`, `~/x.txt`, `/tmp/e-1.md` (gone or present),
  a bare `foo.md` as the whole value.
- Rule 2 blocks: `See /tmp/x.md for detail`; `the plan lives at /Users/x/plan.md`
  inside an otherwise-long paragraph; a multiline value with an absolute path on
  any line.
- Allowed: relative refs mid-content (`edit internal/hookcmd/claude.go then …`,
  `notes in ./foo.md`); multiline content whose only paths are relative; prose with
  no path.
- `--allow-path` exempts: `--text "see /opt/corp/spec.md" --allow-path '^/opt/corp/'`
  → allowed; a second, non-matching absolute path in the same content still blocks.

## Deliverable 2 — Data repair

One-shot repair (a script, not an auto-migration — this is a ledger content fix;
land per the ledger-hygiene-direct-to-main path, not a user worktree). Scan every
inline multiline column for a corrupted value — Rule 1's predicate (the whole
value is a single path token) OR Rule 2's (contains an absolute path):
- `tasks`: `text`, `description`, `analysis`, `outcome` (and `notes` if it can be
  set from an inline flag).
- `decisions`: `description` (+ any other inline multiline columns).

For each hit, recover content in priority order:
1. Committed mirror `.endless/plans/E-NNN.md` — in the worktree, on `main`, or in
   git history (`git log --all -- .endless/plans/E-NNN.md`, then
   `git show <sha>:<path>`).
2. The referenced path itself, if it still exists on disk.
3. Otherwise report the row as **UNRECOVERABLE** for manual attention.

Emit a per-row report (recovered-from / unrecoverable). Do NOT silently drop
unrecoverable rows — surface them. Known unrecoverable at filing: E-1626.text
(re-verify against git `--all` first).

## Deliverable 3 — Docs / guides / error-message sweep (stop teaching it)

`grep` the repo for guidance that passes a path to an inline flag and fix each to
the `--xxxx-file` form (or clarify inline-vs-file):
- Guide markdown and the `endless guide` source, spawn-prompt templates, any
  `CLAUDE.md` snippets, and `*.py` Click help/error strings.
- Patterns: `--text <`, `--outcome <`, `--description <`, `--analysis <` followed
  by a path-looking token.
- Coordinate with the E-1202 gate message (already corrected to `--text-file`) and
  note that the E-1202 task *description* still contains the wrong `--text` form.

## Deliverable 4 — Generate the verify script (do NOT hand-verify)

As part of this task, the implementing session GENERATES
`tests/tasks/e-1744-verify.sh` (self-contained, sandbox DB, `uv run endless` — no
build; shape/output per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`, "ALL PASSED" or a failure
list). It must cover, at minimum:
- **Rule 1 blocks** (whole value is a path): a bare path to `--text`, `--outcome`,
  `--description`, `--analysis` (via `task update` AND `task add`) → refused, output
  names the matching `--xxx-file`. Include a nonexistent path (still blocked).
- **Rule 2 blocks** (absolute path anywhere): `See /tmp/x.md for detail`; an
  absolute path buried in a long paragraph (`… the plan is at /Users/x/plan.md …`);
  a multiline value with an absolute path on any line → refused.
- **Allowed (must stay green)**: `--text-file <real file>`; **relative** paths
  mid-content (`edit internal/hookcmd/claude.go then …`, `notes in ./foo.md`);
  multiline content whose only paths are relative; a plain inline note with no path.
- **Escape hatch**: `--text "see /opt/corp/spec.md" --allow-path '^/opt/corp/'` →
  allowed; a second non-matching absolute path in the same content still blocks;
  `--allow-path` repeatable.
- **Built-in allowed paths**: a path under endless's config or cache dir (e.g.
  `--text "the DB is at ~/.config/endless/endless.db"`) is allowed WITHOUT
  `--allow-path`; verify it still passes when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` are
  set (resolved, not hardcoded).
- **Docs sweep**: no `--<inline-flag> <path>` guidance remains in `docs/` or the
  guide/help source.
- **Data repair**: the one-shot repair is a separate script that emits its own
  recovered/unrecoverable report — reference it in the handoff for a manual eyeball
  rather than re-running it inside the verify script.

Commit the verify script with the implementation.

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

On completion, set `unverified` and tell Mike to run exactly:

```
esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1744-verify.sh
```

Do not hand-verify on Mike's behalf; the script is the verification.

## Notes

- Relates to the E-1202 preToolUse gate (a Claude-hook gate on plan-mirror file
  writes); this task is the complementary **CLI-layer** gate on the flag *value*,
  plus the data/doc cleanup the corruption made necessary. Complemented by the
  multiline-mirror task (durability) and the `/tmp`→`.endless/tmp` task (sanctioned
  scratch dir).
- Both rules hard-block (Mike): Rule 1 = the whole value IS a path (absolute or
  relative — the mis-passed-file case); Rule 2 = the content contains an ABSOLUTE
  path anywhere. Relative paths mid-content are always allowed (plans reference
  project-relative source paths constantly). `--allow-path=<regex>` (repeatable) is
  the escape hatch for a genuine absolute path.
- The verify script is a deliverable of THIS task (Deliverable 4), generated by
  the implementing session — not pre-authored.

   NOT `events.commitPaths`, which refuses linked worktrees (`ensureMainCheckout`).
   Zero new files → no commit.

Re-runnable and idempotent (gap-fill means a second run finds every file present
and writes nothing). Precedent for a persisted, re-runnable backfill driver:
`tests/tasks/e-1719-backfill.sh`.

## Scope

- Fields: all four — text, outcome, analysis, decision bodies.
- Project: the worktree's project only (endless). Other projects, if they adopt
  the committed-mirror convention, run their own backfill later — out of scope.

## Deliverable — verify script

Generate `tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh` (isolated env, shape per
`tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh`). Seed a project + a git worktree; create tasks
carrying outcome/analysis (and text) with NO per-task worktree, plus a decision;
run the backfill from the worktree via
`go run .endless/migrations/e-1754-backfill-doc-mirrors.go`. Assert:
- the expected `.endless/{plans,outcomes,analyses}/E-NNN.md` and
  `.endless/decisions/ED-NNN.md` appear in the worktree AND are in one commit.
- a task/decision with empty fields produces no file.
- an already-present mirror is left untouched (gap-fill, not overwrite).
- re-running the backfill makes no second commit (idempotent).

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

Set `unverified`; tell Mike to run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1754-verify.sh`.
MANUAL: in the real E-1754 worktree, run the backfill; `git log`/`git status`
show one `backfill doc mirrors` commit with the expected new files; then land
E-1754 normally and confirm the mirrors arrive on main.

## Notes

- Reuses E-1747: the field→subdir convention and file layout; `internal/monitor`
  for reads. The genuinely new piece is the bulk read + single worktree-branch
  commit, packaged as a build-excluded one-off (no command surface).
- Not a legacy command: nothing is added to `endless` / `endless-go`. The
  artifact persists like a dated migration and is re-runnable via `go run`.

fields.analysis:
Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; proposed, not yet decided):

The `git branch --merged main` test catches only FULLY-merged branches. It
misses the common re-land failure where a branch's commit was `git commit
--amend`-ed AFTER its content had already been landed: the branch is then a
partial duplicate of main plus a new delta — not fully merged — so `--merged`
is false and land proceeds into a source-file rebase conflict.

Proposed gate (reuses task_landings, which already records each landing's SHA):
on a re-land (task has >=1 task_landings row), require the branch HEAD to be a
descendant of the last landed SHA:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor <last_landed_sha> HEAD

A correct follow-up (a new commit stacked on a branch first rebased onto main)
passes, because main contains that SHA. An amend/rewrite of the already-landed
commit fails the check. On failure, refuse BEFORE the rebase mutates anything
and print the accurate cause + recovery (the reset+reapply path detailed on
E-1417) rather than today's misleading E-972 auto-file message.

Concrete repro: E-1750's first commit was landed; a follow-up (a legend
addition) was made by amending that commit instead of stacking a new one; the
next `just land` rebase re-applied the whole change onto a main that already
had it -> CONFLICT in internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go. Recovery was
manual reset-to-main + re-apply-delta. Couples to E-1417 (the diagnosis half).

Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; proposed, not yet decided):

A third conflict cause, distinct from the two this task already names (the
orphan-cleanup rebase, and main-moved-with-independent-changes): the branch
commit RE-INTRODUCES content already landed for this task — typically a
`git commit --amend` of a commit that was already landed. Today `just land`
misattributes this to the E-972 auto-file routing rule and suggests
`git checkout main -- .endless/*.jsonl`, which cannot fix a source-file conflict.

For THIS cause the recovery is NOT "resolve + git rebase --continue" (that
produces a duplicated commit). It is: capture the new delta, reset the branch to
main, re-apply only the delta:

    git diff main..HEAD -- <source files> > delta.patch
    git reset --hard main && git apply delta.patch && git commit

Detection: inspect the conflicted paths. If any is a source (non-auto) file AND
the branch is not a descendant of the task's last task_landings SHA (see E-1308's
proposed gate), report the amend/rewrite cause and the reset+reapply recovery
instead of the auto-file message.

Concrete repro: E-1750 (see E-1308).

payload.title: Reopen a done task to revisit automatically when its plan text is edited
payload.description: Editing tasks.text on a task in a done state (assumed/confirmed/completed) adds unshipped scope, making the done-status a lie and leaving the task hidden from session monitor. Today the agent must remember to set revisit by hand — the wrong layer in a product used across many projects. Have task update auto-transition a done task to revisit (and announce it) when its plan text actually changes; scoped to text edits (not outcome/analysis), with a --keep-status escape hatch. Replaces relying on agent memory.
payload.text:
# Auto-set a done task to `revisit` when its plan text is edited — PLAN

## Context
Editing the plan (`tasks.text`) of a task that is already in a done state adds
unshipped scope, so the done-status becomes a lie AND the task stays hidden from
session monitor. Today the fix is manual (an agent must remember to run
`task update <id> --status revisit`). In a product used across ~40 projects, that
depends on every agent/user remembering — the wrong layer. Make the CLI do it.

Surfaced when E-1744 (status `assumed`) gained built-in allowed-paths scope and had
to be hand-flipped to `revisit`.

## Behavior
In `update_plan` (`src/endless/task_cmd.py`): when a `task update` changes
`tasks.text` AND the task's current status is a *successfully-done* terminal state,
auto-transition status → `revisit` and ANNOUNCE it (e.g. "E-NNN was assumed; plan
text changed → status set to revisit").

## Design decisions (confirm with Mike)
1. **Which statuses trigger it** — recommend the *completed-successfully* set:
   `assumed`, `confirmed`, `completed`. EXCLUDE the *abandoned* set (`obsolete`,
   `declined`): editing an obsolete task's plan is usually doc cleanup, not a
   revival, and auto-reviving would be surprising. Confirm.
2. **Trigger field** — `tasks.text` (the plan) ONLY. Editing `--outcome` /
   `--analysis` / `--description` on a done task is normal (recording results) and
   must NOT reopen it.
3. **Only on real change** — diff existing vs incoming text; an identical re-write
   is a no-op (no flip).
4. **Escape hatch** — a `--keep-status` flag to suppress the auto-flip for a pure
   typo/formatting edit. Recommend including it. Confirm the name.
5. **Epics are special** — flipping an EPIC to `revisit` triggers the E-1542
   pause-on-revisit gate for every in-flight descendant session. That may be
   intended (the epic's strategy changed) or too blunt for a plan tweak. Decide
   whether epics auto-flip like leaves, or are excluded / warned instead.

## On completion
Prune `feedback_revisit_resurfaces_in_monitor.md` and its `MEMORY.md` line — the
behavior is now automatic, so the memory (interim reinforcement) is obsolete.

## Deliverable — verify script
Generate `tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh` (shape per `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`,
sandbox DB): editing `--text` on an `assumed` task flips it to `revisit` and
announces; identical-text re-write does NOT flip; `--outcome` edit on a done task
does NOT flip; `--keep-status` suppresses; a non-done task (e.g. `underway`) is
unaffected. On completion set `unverified` and hand off exactly:
`esu && ./tests/tasks/e-<id>-verify.sh`.

fields.text:
# E-1417 — Report rebase-conflict causes accurately in `worktree land`

## Context

`endless worktree land` rebases a task branch in two places, and BOTH miscategorize
a conflict — sending the user to the wrong step with the wrong fix:

- **Step 3.7** — `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits` (runs only when the branch has
  contiguous auto-amend orphan commits at its base). Its `rebase --onto base
  last_orphan` both drops the orphans AND replays the user's commits; a conflict in
  the replay raises `orphan auto-amend cleanup failed: <stderr blob>`, which names
  the wrong step (the drop succeeded — the replay conflicted) and buries the
  conflicting filenames in stderr.
- **Step 4** — the main `git rebase base` (runs when there are no base orphans). A
  conflict raises `rebase … failed. Likely cause: … an endless-managed auto-file
  (E-972) … git checkout main -- <globs>`. This is a **confident misattribution**:
  a real source-file conflict gets the auto-file story and a recovery that cannot
  work.

Observed repro: the E-1750 land hit Step 4 with a conflict in
`internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go`; the message told the user to
`git checkout main -- .endless/*.jsonl`, which was irrelevant, turning a
copy-paste recovery into a debugging session.

Both messages also cite internal task IDs (E-972, E-1019) in user-facing text,
which the house rule forbids.

## Goal

On a rebase conflict in either step, report the **facts** confidently — which step,
which files — and present the plausible recoveries as **candidates to judge
between**, explicitly flagged as possibly-wrong, never a single confident
prescription. `land` stays non-interactive and stateless (it still aborts the
rebase). Decided with Mike 2026-07-10: approach (a) detect-and-present-candidates,
covering BOTH Step 3.7 and Step 4 via one shared helper (families b/c rejected —
see this task's analysis).

## Implementation

### 1. Shared conflict-message builder
Add to `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py`:

    def _rebase_conflict_message(worktree_path, base_branch, *, phase) -> str

Called from BOTH handlers while the rebase is still in progress (before any
`git rebase --abort`). It:
- Reads the unmerged paths: `git -C <wt> diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`.
- Optionally names the commit that failed to replay (`git -C <wt> rev-parse
  --short REBASE_HEAD` + its subject) so the user knows which of their commits
  hit the conflict.
- Classifies each conflicting path as auto-file (via the existing
  `AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS` / `DB_LEDGER_DIR` matcher near `worktree_cmd.py:570`) vs
  source.
- Builds the message per §3.

### 2. Wire both call sites
- Step 3.7 handler (the `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` around
  `_drop_orphan_amendable_commits`): build the message with
  `phase="replaying your commits after dropping base auto-amend commits"`, THEN
  `git rebase --abort`, then `raise click.ClickException(msg)`.
- Step 4 handler (the `except` around `git rebase base_branch`): same, with
  `phase="rebasing your branch onto <base>"`. Delete the hardcoded auto-file
  cause and the E-972/E-1019 citations.

### 3. Message contract (this is the acceptance spec)
- Names the real step (the `phase` text), never "orphan cleanup" for a replay
  conflict.
- Lists each conflicting file on its own physical line.
- Every copyable git command on ONE physical line. No emojis. **No `E-NNN`
  internal task IDs.**
- **Auto-file-only** (every conflicting path is an auto-file): high confidence →
  the auto-file recovery (`git -C <wt> checkout <base> -- <globs>`, then retry).
- **Source conflict** (any conflicting path is a source file): a header that the
  cause is uncertain — e.g. "Likely causes (inspect and choose; the wrong
  recovery can duplicate or lose work):" — followed by ≥2 candidates:
  1. *main advanced with overlapping edits*: `cd <wt>` ; `git rebase <base>` ;
     resolve ; `git rebase --continue` ; retry land.
  2. *the branch re-introduces already-landed content* (e.g. an amended
     already-landed commit): capture the delta, `git reset --hard <base>`,
     re-apply only the delta, commit ; retry.
  Plus inspect lines: `git -C <wt> log <base>..HEAD` and
  `git -C <wt> diff <base>...HEAD`.
- Always aborts the rebase after building the message.

### Files
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — add `_rebase_conflict_message`; rewrite the two
  `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` handlers (Step 3.7 and Step 4).

## Tests
- New `tests/test_worktree_land_conflict_msg.py` — unit-tests `_rebase_conflict_message`
  against crafted tmp git repos (reuse the real-git-repo pattern from
  `tests/test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`): a **source** conflict → message names
  the file(s) + ≥2 candidate recoveries + no auto-file-only prescription; an
  **auto-file-only** conflict → the auto-file recovery; the two `phase` strings
  produce distinct step naming; output contains no `E-` token.
- Existing `test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py` stays green.

## Verify
`tests/tasks/e-1417-verify.sh` — handoff is exactly:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1417-verify.sh

It drives `_rebase_conflict_message` headlessly against crafted git repos (no full
land machinery), asserting the §3 contract for the source-conflict and
auto-file-only cases and the no-`E-NNN` rule. It is RED until this task is
implemented (helper absent → reported as a clear failure, not a crash) and GREEN
after.

## Coordination / non-goals
- E-1308 is the PREVENTIVE gate (refuse an already-landed re-land before the
  rebase); this task is the DIAGNOSIS after a conflict. Complementary — the
  "already-landed" candidate here mirrors E-1308's recovery.
- E-1416 (sibling: uncommitted-artifact land failure) — share this message style
  if it lands first.
- Out of scope: auto-resolving conflicts; making `land` interactive/stateful
  (rules out families b/c); changing orphan-detection logic.

fields.analysis:
Approach decision (with Mike, 2026-07-10): family (a) detect-and-present-
candidates, covering BOTH conflict sites (Step 3.7 orphan-replay + Step 4 main
rebase) via one shared message helper. Rejected alternatives:
- (b) leave-in-conflict (don't abort; user resolves + `git rebase --continue` +
  re-runs land): makes land stateful and re-entrant (verbs.json dedup on re-entry,
  user-self-abort races). Land is non-interactive by contract — rejected.
- (c) split the orphan-drop and user-commit replay into two rebases for structural
  attribution: extra rebase + its own rollback handling for marginal gain over
  reading the conflict state — rejected.
Key refinement from Mike: the recovery must be presented as CANDIDATES flagged as
possibly-incorrect, not one confident prescription. The current Step 4 message's
confident-but-wrong "auto-file" recovery is exactly the failure mode to avoid (it
misdirected the E-1750 land). Report facts confidently (step + files); offer
recoveries humbly.

Scope note: the original filing targeted only Step 3.7's "orphan auto-amend
cleanup failed" message and assumed Step 4's message was the good one to borrow.
The E-1750 land proved Step 4's message is ALSO wrong (confident auto-file
misattribution), so the fix covers both.

---

Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; folded into the plan's source-conflict
candidates): the branch commit RE-INTRODUCES content already landed for this task
— typically a `git commit --amend` of a commit that was already landed. Today
`just land` misattributes this to the E-972 auto-file rule and suggests
`git checkout main -- .endless/*.jsonl`, which cannot fix a source-file conflict.
For THIS cause the recovery is NOT "resolve + git rebase --continue" (that
duplicates the commit). It is: capture the new delta, reset the branch to base,
re-apply only the delta:

    git diff main..HEAD -- <source files> > delta.patch
    git reset --hard main && git apply delta.patch && git commit

Detection: if any conflicting path is a source (non-auto) file AND the branch is
not a descendant of the task's last task_landings SHA (see E-1308's proposed
gate), this cause is likely. Concrete repro: E-1750 (see E-1308).

fields.text:
# E-1758 — Worktree anomaly check: `worktree check` (agent) + `session status` detail (human)

## Context

The handoff prompt tells agents to "report git/worktree side-effects (uncommitted
changes, dangling tags, stray artifacts), the landed-vs-worktree delta" — an
enumeration of categories. Naming an empty category makes the agent fill it with
"none," so a clean handoff produces "nothing to report" dressed as reporting.
Two of the named categories aren't even real: endless **never creates git tags**
("dangling tags" is a non-problem), and a pre-land branch **normally** has commits
ahead of main (the work), so "landed-vs-worktree delta" is the expected state, not
an anomaly.

Fix: compute the *real* anomalies so a clean state is **silence**, not prose.
Surface it two ways (Mike's steer — both, not either/or):
- `endless worktree check` — the agent runs it at handoff; prints nothing when
  clean, terse anomaly lines otherwise.
- `endless session status` — the same anomalies rendered inline so Mike sees git
  state directly (today it shows only the coarse ◆ dirty marker, not *what*).

Both consume ONE definition of "anomaly" so they never disagree.

## Anomaly set (single source of truth)

Report ONLY genuine handoff anomalies:
- Uncommitted or untracked **user** files — `git status --porcelain`, partitioned
  to exclude endless's own auto-managed files (the globs `_git_status_partition`
  already uses: db-ledger, plans/outcomes/analyses/decisions mirrors, verbs.jsonl,
  companion, `.claude/settings.json`). Endless-managed dirt alone → still clean.
- HEAD **detached**, or not on the worktree's companion `branch`.
- The worktree (or a sibling e-NNN dir) **prunable / stale-locked / leaked**.

Explicitly NOT anomalies (stay silent):
- Commits ahead of main (expected before land).
- Git tags (endless never creates them).

Empty anomaly list ⇒ clean ⇒ no output.

## Mechanism

**Shared core (Go).** Generalize `monitor.taskWorktreeDirty` (currently a bool that
collapses dirty-or-unlanded) into `monitor.WorktreeAnomalies(...)` returning a typed
list (kind + short detail), computed via the existing `runGit`, the reaper's
`git worktree list --porcelain` prunable/lock inspection, and a
centralized auto-managed-file glob (port the list currently living behind Python's
`_git_status_partition` into one shared Go definition so both languages agree). The
"unlanded commits" branch of `taskWorktreeDirty` is dropped from the anomaly list
per the silence rule (the ◆ marker's unlanded meaning can stay as-is for the
navigation view).

**Surface 1 — `endless worktree check` (agent).** New subcommand in the Python
`worktree` group; resolves the current worktree from cwd (reuse `current_worktree`
/ `worktree_root_for_cwd`), shells to a Go subcommand (e.g.
`endless-go session-query worktree-anomalies --task-id N`, matching the existing
session-query pattern), prints one line per anomaly, nothing when empty. Exit 0 when
clean, non-zero when anomalies (scriptable; the agent relays stdout verbatim).

**Surface 2 — `session status` detail.** Extend the Go render
(`SessionStatusRow` / `AnnotateSessionStatusDirty` in `internal/sessionstatuscmd` +
`internal/monitor`) so the ◆ marker expands to the same `WorktreeAnomalies`
breakdown for the focal worktree — silent (unchanged output) when there are none.

## Scope boundary

E-1758 delivers the shared core + both surfaces + the glob centralization. It does
NOT rewrite the handoff templates (that is E-1759, which will wire `worktree check`
into all six `internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/*.tmpl` and strike the
"dangling tags" / "landed-vs-worktree delta" language) and does NOT add the lint
gate (E-1760).

## Deliverable — verify script

Generate `tests/tasks/e-1758-verify.sh` (isolated env + a real worktree, shape per
`tests/tasks/e-1747-verify.sh`). Assert:
- clean worktree → `endless worktree check` prints nothing, exit 0.
- an untracked USER file → printed, exit non-zero.
- an endless auto-managed file alone (e.g. a `.endless/outcomes/E-NNN.md`) → still
  clean (partitioned out).
- commits ahead of main with an otherwise-clean tree → still clean (silence rule).
- detached HEAD → flagged.
- `session status` shows the same detail behind ◆ when dirty, and nothing extra
  when clean.
Plus Go unit tests for `WorktreeAnomalies` covering each anomaly kind + the clean
case.

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

Set `unverified`; run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1758-verify.sh`.

## Notes

- Reuses E-1701's ◆-marker git-cost pattern (`taskWorktreeDirty`) and the Python
  `worktree` inspection helpers; the one genuinely new asset is the typed
  `WorktreeAnomalies` core and its single auto-managed glob definition.
- Once landed, unblocks E-1759 (templates call `worktree check`) and complements
  E-1760 (the lint gate catches ceremony the template can't).

payload.title: Replace hardcoded "Mike" with "the user" in user-facing docs; add a regression guard
payload.description: User-facing docs must say 'the user', not a hardcoded name. Two shipped instructional surfaces (docs/guide/sessions.md, docs/TASK_RECORDING_PROMPT.md) hardcode 'Mike'; fix them and add a permanent guard test so it cannot regress. Pre-existing, surfaced while landing E-1648.
payload.text:
User-facing docs must refer to "the user", never a hardcoded name. Two shipped instructional surfaces currently hardcode "Mike":

1. docs/guide/sessions.md:34 — an example task line reads `waiting on Mike's review`. Change to `waiting on the user's review` (or `waiting on user review`). This ships via `endless guide sessions`, so other users/agents read it.
2. docs/TASK_RECORDING_PROMPT.md — two lines: "...until Mike notices and asks" and "Do this without Mike having to remind, prompt, or catch omissions". Reword to "the user".

Then add a guard so this cannot regress: a permanent test (in `just test`, e.g. tests/test_docs_no_hardcoded_name.py) that scans the user-facing docs — docs/guide/*.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/TASK_RECORDING_PROMPT.md — for the token "Mike" and fails with file:line if found.

Scope note — the guard must NOT flag legitimate uses: Go/SQL code comments that attribute design decisions to the actual person ("decided with Mike", "Per Mike's ..."), and the personal author/speaker docs docs/brief-*.md and docs/talk-*.md (Mike is genuinely the author there). Keep the guard limited to the user-facing instructional surfaces listed above, and exclude docs/private (git-excluded). Surfaced 2026-07-10 while landing E-1648; pre-existing, independent of the submitted-status work.
